The top 30 fall into three groups.

**Stromal matrix remodeling.** Cancer-associated fibroblasts are the main senders of collagens and fibronectin. Their receptors include syndecan-1 (SDC1) on other fibroblasts, integrin α1β1 (`ITGA1_ITGB1`) on perivascular cells, and integrin α5β1 (`ITGA5_ITGB1`) on endothelial cells. The collagen pathway alone contributes 61 interactions with a mean priority of 0.81.

**Chemokine signaling at the endothelium and in T cells.** Endothelial ACKR1 receives CCL5 from T cells and CXCL8 from myeloid cells. ACKR1 is an atypical receptor that transports chemokines across the endothelium without signaling through G proteins. Fibroblast-derived CXCL12 reaches CXCR4 on T and B cells.

**Antigen presentation and related immune interfaces.** Myeloid MHC-II molecules pair with CD4, endothelial COL4A1 pairs with CD44 on myeloid cells, and endothelial APP pairs with CD74 on B and myeloid cells.

The consensus set is a list of candidates for follow-up, not a list of validated mechanisms.

## Prioritization and the adhesion-receptor rule

The top of the list is dominated by collagen and fibronectin pairs that bind CD44 or syndecan-1. Promiscuous matrix receptors of this kind recur across many ligands and sender types, and they mostly describe the desmoplastic stroma in general. We are interested in receptor-specific axes, so we apply a filter to every interaction before ranking. The filter is a rule, written down after the original curation, which it formalizes. It does not depend on where any single interaction ranks, and the variants below show how much the selection depends on it:

> An interaction is excluded if its receptor is a single-chain receptor (not a multi-subunit complex in CellChatDB) that binds at least 10 distinct ligands through extracellular-matrix-receptor interactions in CellChatDB.

The rule flags CD44, SDC1, SDC4, GP6, DAG1 and SV2A/B/C. The next single-chain matrix receptors, CD36 and CD47, bind 5 ligands each, so the threshold sits at a clear gap. Integrin α5β1 is a heterodimer with one matrix ligand in CellChatDB and passes. After the rule, the five axes in the table below rank first to fifth. For APP-CD74 the highest-ranked instance has myeloid receivers; the downstream single-cell and spatial analyses use its endothelial-to-B-cell instance, which is also in the consensus set (eighth after the rule), and the comparison with normal tissue shows both.

```{r}
#| label: axes-setup
#| eval: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Candidate Registry Definition
candidate_registry <- tibble::tribble(
  ~axis_id, ~ligand, ~receptor, ~sender_celltype, ~receiver_celltype,
  "cxcl12_cxcr4", "CXCL12", "CXCR4", "Fibroblast", "T_cell",
  "ccl5_ackr1", "CCL5", "ACKR1", "T_cell", "Endothelial",
  "mdk_lrp1", "MDK", "LRP1", "Fibroblast", "Fibroblast",
  "fn1_itga5_itgb1", "FN1", "ITGA5_ITGB1", "Fibroblast", "Endothelial",
  "app_cd74", "APP", "CD74", "Endothelial", "B_cell"
)

knitr::kable(
  candidate_registry %>% dplyr::select(ligand, receptor, sender_celltype, receiver_celltype),
  digits = 4,
  caption = "The five candidate axes carried into the downstream analyses, with the sender and receiver used downstream."
)
```

```{r}
#| label: rev-prioritisation
#| eval: true
cons <- read_csv("results/cross_cohort_comparison/consensus_interactions_all.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
db_int <- CellChat::CellChatDB.human$interaction
db_cx <- CellChat::CellChatDB.human$complex

receptor_props <- db_int %>%
  group_by(receptor) %>%
  summarise(
    n_ligands = n_distinct(ligand),
    n_ecm_ligands = n_distinct(ligand[annotation == "ECM-Receptor"]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(is_complex = receptor %in% rownames(db_cx))
receptor_subunits <- lapply(setNames(receptor_props$receptor, receptor_props$receptor), function(r) {
  if (r %in% rownames(db_cx)) {
    s <- unlist(db_cx[r, grep("^subunit", colnames(db_cx))])
    s[s != ""]
  } else {
    r
  }
})

fails_rule <- function(threshold, include_complexes = FALSE) {
  receptor_props$receptor[receptor_props$n_ecm_ligands >= threshold & (include_complexes | !receptor_props$is_complex)]
}
failing_main <- fails_rule(10)
failing_t5 <- fails_rule(5)
failing_complex <- fails_rule(10, include_complexes = TRUE)
failing_subunits <- unique(unlist(receptor_subunits[failing_complex]))
failing_subunit_level <- receptor_props$receptor[vapply(receptor_props$receptor, function(r) any(receptor_subunits[[r]] %in% failing_subunits), logical(1))]

prio <- cons %>%
  mutate(
    score_no_drug = (Cons_Score + Agree_Score) / 2,
    rank_uncurated = rank(-Priority, ties.method = "min"),
    rank_uncurated_no_drug = rank(-score_no_drug, ties.method = "min"),
    pass_main = !Receptor %in% failing_main,
    pass_t5 = !Receptor %in% failing_t5,
    pass_complex = !Receptor %in% failing_complex,
    pass_subunit = !Receptor %in% failing_subunit_level
  )
rank_within <- function(score, pass) {
  out <- rep(NA_integer_, length(score))
  out[pass] <- rank(-score[pass], ties.method = "min")
  out
}
prio <- prio %>%
  mutate(
    rank_rule = rank_within(Priority, pass_main),
    rank_rule_no_drug = rank_within(score_no_drug, pass_main),
    rank_rule_t5 = rank_within(Priority, pass_t5),
    rank_rule_complex = rank_within(Priority, pass_complex),
    rank_rule_subunit = rank_within(Priority, pass_subunit)
  )
write_csv(prio, "results/revision/prioritisation_all_interactions.csv")

axis_keys <- candidate_registry %>%
  transmute(axis_id, Source = sender_celltype, Target = ifelse(axis_id == "app_cd74", "Myeloid", receiver_celltype), Ligand = ligand, Receptor = receptor)
axis_ranks <- axis_keys %>%
  left_join(prio, by = c("Source", "Target", "Ligand", "Receptor")) %>%
  transmute(
    Axis = axis_labels[axis_id], Source, Target, Priority = round(Priority, 3), `Score without druggability` = round(score_no_drug, 3),
    `Rank (uncurated)` = rank_uncurated, `Rank (uncurated, no druggability)` = rank_uncurated_no_drug,
    `Rank (rule)` = rank_rule, `Rank (rule, no druggability)` = rank_rule_no_drug,
    `Rank (threshold 5)` = rank_rule_t5, `Rank (rule incl. complexes)` = rank_rule_complex, `Rank (subunit-level)` = rank_rule_subunit
  )
write_csv(axis_ranks, "results/revision/prioritisation_axis_ranks.csv")
knitr::kable(axis_ranks, caption = sprintf("Rank of the five axes among the %d consensus interactions, with and without druggability and under the adhesion-receptor rule and its variants", nrow(prio)))

rule_summary <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Variant, ~`Failing receptors in CellChatDB`, ~`Interactions removed`, ~`Lead receptors failing`,
  "Main rule (single-chain, >= 10 ECM ligands)", paste(sort(failing_main), collapse = ", "), sum(!prio$pass_main), paste(intersect(candidate_registry$receptor, failing_main), collapse = ", "),
  "Threshold 5", paste(sort(failing_t5), collapse = ", "), sum(!prio$pass_t5), paste(intersect(candidate_registry$receptor, failing_t5), collapse = ", "),
  "Rule extended to complexes", paste(sort(intersect(failing_complex, prio$Receptor)), collapse = ", "), sum(!prio$pass_complex), paste(intersect(candidate_registry$receptor, failing_complex), collapse = ", "),
  "Subunit-level", paste(sort(intersect(failing_subunit_level, prio$Receptor)), collapse = ", "), sum(!prio$pass_subunit), paste(intersect(candidate_registry$receptor, failing_subunit_level), collapse = ", ")
)
write_csv(rule_summary, "results/revision/prioritisation_rule_summary.csv")
knitr::kable(rule_summary, caption = "Adhesion-receptor rule and sensitivity variants")

knitr::kable(
  tibble::tibble(
    `Druggable interactions` = sum(prio$Therap_Score == 1),
    `Druggable in top 30` = sum(head(prio$Therap_Score[order(-prio$Priority)], 30) == 1),
    `Spearman rho, score with vs without druggability` = round(cor(prio$Priority, prio$score_no_drug, method = "spearman"), 3)
  ),
  caption = "Druggability term in the composite score"
)

knitr::kable(
  prio %>% filter(pass_main) %>% arrange(rank_rule) %>% head(15) %>%
    select(rank_rule, rank_uncurated, rank_rule_no_drug, Source, Target, Ligand, Receptor, Pathway, Priority, score_no_drug),
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Top 15 interactions after the adhesion-receptor rule"
)
```

The druggability term does not drive the ranking. Without it, the five axes keep their ranks (CCL5-ACKR1 5, APP-CD74 6, CXCL12-CXCR4 7, MDK-LRP1 12, FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1 15 of 209), and the Spearman correlation between the scores with and without the term is 0.82. Before the rule is applied, the five axes occupy ranks 5 to 15, which is already near the top of 209. After it, they take ranks 1 to 5, with CCL5-ACKR1 first, APP-CD74 second, CXCL12-CXCR4 third, MDK-LRP1 fourth and FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1 fifth. A lower threshold (5 ligands), extending the rule to multi-subunit receptors, and the subunit-level variant do not change the order of the first four, and the first two variants also keep FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1 fifth. Under the subunit-level variant `ITGA5_ITGB1` fails through `ITGB1`, a promiscuous β subunit that it shares with the α1β1 and α6β1 integrins. We keep the axis, because the rule is applied to the functional heterodimer.

The five axes are the five carried into the rest of the analysis. All five are conserved in all three cohorts and are found by both frameworks.

```{r}
#| label: rev-consensus-regeneration
#| eval: true
#| include: false
cons_pub <- read_csv("results/revision/published_208_backup/consensus_interactions_all.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(rank_published = rank(-Priority, ties.method = "min"))
cons_new <- cons %>% mutate(rank_regenerated = rank(-Priority, ties.method = "min"))
cons_change <- full_join(
  cons_pub %>% select(Source, Target, Ligand, Receptor, priority_published = Priority, rank_published),
  cons_new %>% select(Source, Target, Ligand, Receptor, priority_regenerated = Priority, rank_regenerated),
  by = c("Source", "Target", "Ligand", "Receptor")
) %>%
  mutate(status = case_when(is.na(priority_published) ~ "added", is.na(priority_regenerated) ~ "removed", TRUE ~ "retained"),
         priority_change = priority_regenerated - priority_published) %>%
  arrange(rank_regenerated)
write_csv(cons_change, "results/revision/consensus_published_vs_regenerated.csv")
knitr::kable(
  tibble::tibble(earlier = nrow(cons_pub), current = nrow(cons_new), added = sum(cons_change$status == "added"),
                 removed = sum(cons_change$status == "removed"),
                 `max |priority change|` = round(max(abs(cons_change$priority_change), na.rm = TRUE), 3),
                 `Spearman rho (retained)` = round(cor(cons_change$priority_published, cons_change$priority_regenerated, use = "complete.obs", method = "spearman"), 3)),
  caption = "Earlier build vs current consensus set"
)
knitr::kable(cons_change %>% filter(status != "retained" | rank_regenerated <= 30 | rank_published <= 30) %>%
               mutate(across(starts_with("priority"), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
               rename_with(~ sub("published", "earlier", sub("regenerated", "current", .x))),
             caption = "Top-30 interactions and set changes, earlier build vs current")
```

## Robustness to subsampling

Every cohort is subsampled to 20,000 cells, which corresponds to 12% of the Pal cells, 26% of the Wu cells and 66% of the Qian cells, so the retention fraction differs between cohorts. We checked that the consensus set and the axis ranks do not depend on this choice or on the random seed. We re-sketched each cohort from the full harmonized object with the same leverage-score procedure and four configurations, with seeds 1 to 3 each: a common retention fraction of 25% (Pal 40,144, Wu 19,420 and Qian 7,540 cells), a fixed 10,000 cells, a fixed 30,000 cells (Qian is then essentially complete, with 30,000 of its 30,161 cells), and the original 20,000 cells with new seeds. This gives 12 runs per cohort. CellChat and LIANA were rerun with the original settings in each, and the conserved and consensus sets and the composite score were rebuilt as before. Rerunning the seed-123 sketch reproduces the original sketch exactly, as well as the per-cohort CellChat and LIANA results, so the pipeline is deterministic, and all variation below comes from subsampling.

```{r}
#| label: rev-resketch-run
#| eval: false
suppressMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(qs2)
  library(Seurat)
  library(CellChat)
  library(liana)
  library(SingleCellExperiment)
})

n_workers <- min(num_cores, 6)
out_dir <- "objects/revision/resketch"
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

cohorts <- c("pal", "wu", "qian")
seeds <- c(1, 2, 3)

run_cellchat_lr <- function(data_input, meta) {
  cellchat <- createCellChat(object = data_input, meta = meta, group.by = "harmonized_label")
  cellchat@DB <- CellChatDB.human
  cellchat <- subsetData(cellchat)
  cellchat <- identifyOverExpressedGenes(cellchat)
  cellchat <- identifyOverExpressedInteractions(cellchat)
  cellchat <- computeCommunProb(cellchat, raw.use = TRUE)
  cellchat <- filterCommunication(cellchat, min.cells = 10)
  subsetCommunication(cellchat)
}

run_liana_agg <- function(counts, data_input, meta) {
  sce <- SingleCellExperiment(
    assays = list(counts = counts, logcounts = data_input),
    colData = meta
  )
  liana_res <- liana_wrap(
    sce,
    method = c("natmi", "connectome", "logfc", "sca", "cellphonedb"),
    idents_col = "harmonized_label",
    expr_prop = 0.1,
    min_cells = 10,
    permutation.params = list(nperms = 1000)
  )
  liana_aggregate(liana_res)
}

for (cohort in cohorts) {
  message(sprintf("[%s] %s: loading harmonized object", Sys.time(), cohort))
  seu <- qs_read(sprintf("objects/seu_%s_harmonized_20000.qs2", cohort))
  DefaultAssay(seu) <- "RNA"
  n_total <- ncol(seu)
  orig_cells <- colnames(seu[["sketch"]])

  # Leverage scores are recomputed per seed, as SketchData() does internally
  cells_path <- file.path(out_dir, sprintf("sketch_cells_%s.qs2", cohort))
  if (file.exists(cells_path)) {
    sketch_cells <- qs_read(cells_path)
  } else {
    sizes <- c(
      frac25 = round(0.25 * n_total),
      n10k = 10000,
      n20k = 20000,
      n30k = min(30000, n_total)
    )
    sketch_cells <- list()
    for (s in c(123, seeds)) {
      lev_name <- paste0("lev_s", s)
      seu <- LeverageScore(seu, assay = "RNA", seed = s, var.name = lev_name, over.write = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
      lev <- seu[[lev_name]][, 1]
      run_sizes <- if (s == 123) c(n20k = 20000) else sizes
      for (cfg in names(run_sizes)) {
        set.seed(s)
        sketch_cells[[sprintf("%s_s%d", cfg, s)]] <- sample(colnames(seu), size = min(run_sizes[[cfg]], n_total), prob = lev)
      }
    }
    qs_save(sketch_cells, cells_path)
  }
  message(sprintf("[%s] %s: original sketch reproduced = %s", Sys.time(), cohort,
                  setequal(sketch_cells[["n20k_s123"]], orig_cells)))

  counts_all <- GetAssayData(seu, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
  data_all <- GetAssayData(seu, assay = "RNA", layer = "data")
  meta_all <- seu@meta.data
  rm(seu)
  gc()

  run_ids <- names(sketch_cells)
  todo <- run_ids[!file.exists(file.path(out_dir, sprintf("%s_%s.qs2", cohort, run_ids)))]
  parallel::mclapply(todo, function(run_id) {
    cells <- sketch_cells[[run_id]]
    meta <- meta_all[cells, ]
    data_input <- data_all[, cells]
    t0 <- Sys.time()
    cc_df <- run_cellchat_lr(data_input, meta)
    liana_df <- run_liana_agg(counts_all[, cells], data_input, meta)
    qs_save(
      list(cohort = cohort, run_id = run_id, n_cells = length(cells), cc_df = cc_df, liana_df = liana_df,
           minutes = as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "mins"))),
      file.path(out_dir, sprintf("%s_%s.qs2", cohort, run_id))
    )
    message(sprintf("[%s] %s %s done (%d cells)", Sys.time(), cohort, run_id, length(cells)))
    NULL
  }, mc.cores = n_workers, mc.preschedule = FALSE)

  rm(counts_all, data_all, meta_all)
  gc()
}
message(sprintf("[%s] all re-sketch runs finished", Sys.time()))
```

The next step rebuilds the conserved and consensus sets for every run and compares them with the sets from the reference sketch (20,000 cells, seed 123) with the Jaccard index. It also records where each of the five axes ranks in every run, both before and after the adhesion-receptor rule.

```{r}
#| label: rev-resketch-summary
#| eval: true
rs_files <- list.files("objects/revision/resketch", pattern = "^(pal|wu|qian)_.*\\.qs2$", full.names = TRUE)
rs_runs <- lapply(rs_files, qs_read)
rs_index <- tibble::tibble(
  cohort = vapply(rs_runs, `[[`, character(1), "cohort"),
  run_id = vapply(rs_runs, `[[`, character(1), "run_id"),
  n_cells = vapply(rs_runs, `[[`, numeric(1), "n_cells"),
  minutes = vapply(rs_runs, `[[`, numeric(1), "minutes")
)
complete_runs <- rs_index %>% count(run_id) %>% filter(n == 3) %>% pull(run_id)

# TTD gene symbols parsed as in consensus-validation-calculations
ttd_lines <- readLines("data/ext/P2-01-TTD_uniprot_all.txt")
ttd_fields <- lapply(c("^TARGETID", "^UNIPROID", "^TARGNAME", "^TARGTYPE"), function(tag) ttd_lines[grep(tag, ttd_lines)])
ttd_n <- min(lengths(ttd_fields))
ttd_symbols <- str_match(sub("^TARGNAME\\s+", "", ttd_fields[[3]][1:ttd_n]), "\\(([^\\)]+)\\)$")[, 2]

build_consensus <- function(cc_list, liana_list) {
  cc_cons <- bind_rows(cc_list, .id = "cohort") %>%
    group_by(source, target, ligand, receptor, interaction_name) %>%
    summarise(cc_cohort_count = n_distinct(cohort), cc_mean_prob = mean(prob), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(cc_cohort_count >= 2)
  liana_cons <- bind_rows(liana_list, .id = "cohort") %>%
    filter(aggregate_rank <= 0.05) %>%
    rename(ligand = ligand.complex, receptor = receptor.complex) %>%
    group_by(source, target, ligand, receptor) %>%
    summarise(liana_cohort_count = n_distinct(cohort), liana_mean_rank = mean(aggregate_rank), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(liana_cohort_count >= 2, liana_mean_rank <= 0.05)
  merged <- inner_join(cc_cons, liana_cons, by = c("source", "target", "ligand", "receptor"))
  avg_rank <- (rank(-merged$cc_mean_prob) + rank(merged$liana_mean_rank)) / 2
  merged %>%
    mutate(
      conservation_score = (cc_cohort_count + liana_cohort_count) / 6,
      agreement_score = 1 - (avg_rank - 1) / (n() - 1),
      therapeutic_score = as.numeric(vapply(strsplit(receptor, "_"), function(s) any(s %in% ttd_symbols), logical(1))),
      composite = (conservation_score + agreement_score + therapeutic_score) / 3,
      rank_uncurated = rank(-composite, ties.method = "min"),
      rank_rule = rank_within(composite, !receptor %in% failing_main),
      key = paste(source, target, ligand, receptor, sep = " -> ")
    ) %>%
    list(cc_keys = paste(cc_cons$source, cc_cons$target, cc_cons$ligand, cc_cons$receptor, sep = " -> "),
         liana_keys = paste(liana_cons$source, liana_cons$target, liana_cons$ligand, liana_cons$receptor, sep = " -> "),
         consensus = .)
}

jaccard <- function(a, b) length(intersect(a, b)) / length(union(a, b))
# "Published" refers to the earlier tables archived in results/revision/published_208_backup/
pub_dir <- "results/revision/published_208_backup"
orig_cc_keys <- read_csv(file.path(pub_dir, "conserved_interactions_2_of_3.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  transmute(key = paste(source, target, ligand, receptor, sep = " -> ")) %>% pull(key)
orig_liana_keys <- read_csv(file.path(pub_dir, "liana_conserved_all.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(cohort_count >= 2, mean_aggregate_rank <= 0.05) %>%
  transmute(key = paste(source, target, ligand, receptor, sep = " -> ")) %>% pull(key)
orig_cons_keys <- read_csv(file.path(pub_dir, "consensus_interactions_all.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  transmute(key = paste(Source, Target, Ligand, Receptor, sep = " -> ")) %>% pull(key)
axis_key_vec <- setNames(paste(axis_keys$Source, axis_keys$Target, axis_keys$Ligand, axis_keys$Receptor, sep = " -> "), axis_keys$axis_id)

# The published LIANA-conserved table predates the final per-cohort LIANA outputs, so each run is also
# compared with the sets rebuilt from the original sketch (n20k_s123), which isolates the subsampling effect
rebuild_run <- function(rid) {
  runs <- rs_runs[rs_index$run_id == rid]
  names(runs) <- vapply(runs, `[[`, character(1), "cohort")
  c(list(runs = runs), build_consensus(lapply(runs, `[[`, "cc_df"), lapply(runs, `[[`, "liana_df")))
}
ref <- rebuild_run("n20k_s123")

rs_rows <- list()
rs_axis_rows <- list()
for (rid in complete_runs) {
  bc <- rebuild_run(rid)
  runs <- bc$runs
  rs_rows[[rid]] <- tibble::tibble(
    run_id = rid, config = sub("_s[0-9]+$", "", rid), seed = as.integer(sub(".*_s", "", rid)),
    cells_pal = runs$pal$n_cells, cells_wu = runs$wu$n_cells, cells_qian = runs$qian$n_cells,
    n_cc_conserved = length(bc$cc_keys), n_liana_conserved = length(bc$liana_keys), n_consensus = nrow(bc$consensus),
    jaccard_cc = jaccard(bc$cc_keys, orig_cc_keys), jaccard_liana = jaccard(bc$liana_keys, orig_liana_keys),
    jaccard_consensus = jaccard(bc$consensus$key, orig_cons_keys),
    jaccard_cc_rebuilt = jaccard(bc$cc_keys, ref$cc_keys), jaccard_liana_rebuilt = jaccard(bc$liana_keys, ref$liana_keys),
    jaccard_consensus_rebuilt = jaccard(bc$consensus$key, ref$consensus$key)
  )
  rs_axis_rows[[rid]] <- tibble::tibble(run_id = rid, axis_id = names(axis_key_vec), key = unname(axis_key_vec)) %>%
    left_join(bc$consensus %>% select(key, composite, rank_uncurated, rank_rule), by = "key") %>%
    mutate(in_consensus = !is.na(rank_uncurated), n_consensus = nrow(bc$consensus))
}
rs_summary <- bind_rows(rs_rows) %>% mutate(config = factor(config, levels = c("n20k", "n10k", "frac25", "n30k"))) %>% arrange(config, seed)
rs_axis <- bind_rows(rs_axis_rows) %>% left_join(rs_summary %>% select(run_id, config, seed), by = "run_id")
write_csv(rs_summary, "results/revision/resketch_runs.csv")
write_csv(rs_axis, "results/revision/resketch_axis_ranks.csv")
knitr::kable(rs_summary, digits = 3, caption = "Re-sketching runs: conserved and consensus set sizes and Jaccard overlap with the original sets (n20k_s123 = original sketch reproduced)")

rs_axis_wide <- rs_axis %>%
  transmute(run_id, Axis = axis_labels[axis_id], cell = ifelse(in_consensus, sprintf("%d (%d)", rank_uncurated, rank_rule), "absent")) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Axis, values_from = cell)
write_csv(rs_axis_wide, "results/revision/resketch_axis_ranks_wide.csv")
knitr::kable(rs_axis_wide, caption = "Axis rank in every run: uncurated rank (rank after the adhesion-receptor rule)")

knitr::kable(
  rs_axis %>% filter(run_id != "n20k_s123") %>% group_by(Axis = axis_labels[axis_id]) %>%
    summarise(runs = n(), in_consensus = sum(in_consensus), median_rank = median(rank_uncurated, na.rm = TRUE),
              range_rank = paste(range(rank_uncurated, na.rm = TRUE), collapse = "-"),
              median_rank_rule = median(rank_rule, na.rm = TRUE), range_rank_rule = paste(range(rank_rule, na.rm = TRUE), collapse = "-"),
              top5_after_rule = sum(rank_rule <= 5, na.rm = TRUE), top10_after_rule = sum(rank_rule <= 10, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"),
  caption = "Axis stability across the re-sketching runs (original sketch excluded)"
)

```

Across the 12 alternative sketches, the consensus set overlapped the set rebuilt from the reference sketch with Jaccard indices of 0.81 to 0.95, with the lowest agreement at 30,000 cells. At that size LIANA's conserved set is smaller (about 1,130 against about 1,360 interactions), probably because its rank aggregation becomes more stringent with more cells. All five axes remained in the consensus set in every run, and after the adhesion-receptor rule they ranked first to fifth in every run (@fig-resketch-stability). Before the rule their ranks varied within narrow ranges: APP-CD74 4 to 6, CCL5-ACKR1 5 to 6, CXCL12-CXCR4 7 to 8, MDK-LRP1 11 to 14 and FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1 13 to 16. The choice of sketch size does not change which axes are selected.

```{r}
  filter(run_id != "n20k_s123") %>%

p_rs_rank <- p_rs_rank + guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
p_rs <- p_rs_j + p_rs_rank + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
```

# The candidate axes

Five receptor-specific interactions move forward from the prioritized list. All five are conserved in all three cohorts and are detected by both frameworks:

- **CCL5-ACKR1**, from T cells to endothelial cells. ACKR1 is an atypical chemokine receptor that carries chemokines across the endothelium and does not signal through G proteins.
- **FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1**, from fibroblasts to endothelial cells. Fibronectin binds the α5β1 integrin on endothelium.
- **APP-CD74**, from endothelial cells to B and myeloid cells.
- **MDK-LRP1**, an autocrine loop between fibroblasts.
- **CXCL12-CXCR4**, from fibroblasts to T cells.

The chord diagrams show who sends and who receives each axis in each cohort. A node is a cell type and an edge is the pair's communication probability. They show at a glance whether an axis is specific to one sender-receiver pair or spread over several cell types. CCL5-ACKR1 is the most specific: it runs only from T cells to endothelial cells. APP-CD74 is the most promiscuous, with several cell types expressing the ligand and the receptor (@fig-chord-cxcl12_cxcr4-pal and the other tabs of the set).

```{r}
#| label: chord-diagrams
#| eval: true
dir.create("results/cellchat_chords", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

db_interaction <- CellChat::CellChatDB.human$interaction
chord_axes <- list()
for (i in 1:nrow(candidate_registry)) {
  axis_id <- candidate_registry$axis_id[i]
  lig <- candidate_registry$ligand[i]
  rec <- candidate_registry$receptor[i]
  pair_str <- paste0(lig, "_", rec)

  match_row <- db_interaction %>% dplyr::filter(ligand == lig & (receptor == rec | interaction_name == pair_str))
  if (nrow(match_row) == 0) match_row <- db_interaction %>% dplyr::filter(ligand == lig)
  pw <- if (nrow(match_row) > 0) match_row$pathway_name[1] else lig

  chord_axes[[axis_id]] <- list(pathway = pw, pair = pair_str)
}

draw_chord <- function(cohort_name, axis_id) {
  info <- chord_axes[[axis_id]]
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1), mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1))
  CellChat::netVisual_individual(
    cellchat_list[[cohort_name]],
    signaling = info$pathway,
    pairLR.use = info$pair,
    layout = "chord",
    vertex.label.cex = 1.3,
    title.name = NULL
  )
}

for (axis_id in names(chord_axes)) {
  for (cohort_name in names(cellchat_list)) {
    png(sprintf("results/cellchat_chords/chord_%s_%s.png", tolower(cohort_name), axis_id), width = 1400, height = 1400, res = 150)
    draw_chord(cohort_name, axis_id)
    dev.off()
  }
}
```

# Downstream programs

A conserved interaction is only a candidate. To see whether an axis comes with a transcriptional footprint, we look at the cells that would receive the signal and ask what differs between tumors with a high and a low supply of the ligand. We use three readouts. Transcription factor (TF) activity, estimated with decoupleR, describes the regulators that move with the ligand. NicheNet adds prior knowledge about which target genes a ligand is known to regulate. And a per-sample pseudobulk differential expression analysis tests the receiver programs with the tumor sample as the unit of replication.

The unit of replication matters. Tumors, not cells, are the independent observations, and a cell-level test treats thousands of cells from a handful of patients as independent. We therefore define the groups at the level of samples throughout. In each cohort, samples are split at the median of the fraction of sender cells that detect the ligand (samples with at least 10 sender cells), and expression is summed over the receiver cells of each sample (samples with at least 10 receiver cells). The receptor must be detected in at least 2% of the receiver cells of the cohort, otherwise the axis is skipped for that cohort.

## Transcription factor activity

For every cohort and axis, we aggregate the raw counts of the receiver cells of each sample into a log2 counts-per-million profile, and estimate TF activity per sample with the weighted-mean method of decoupleR against the CollecTRI regulons (at least 5 targets per regulon). We then regress each TF activity on the sender ligand and the receiver receptor expression across samples, and take the ligand term and its p-value. Correlations are corrected with the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure across the roughly 765 TFs tested per run. The results are saved in `results/tf_activity/`.

```{r}
#| label: load-seurat-objects
#| eval: false
seu_pal <- qs_read("objects/seu_pal_harmonized_20000.qs2")
seu_wu <- qs_read("objects/seu_wu_harmonized_20000.qs2")
seu_qian <- qs_read("objects/seu_qian_harmonized_20000.qs2")

cc_pal <- qs_read("objects/cc_pal_20000.qs2")
cc_wu <- qs_read("objects/cc_wu_20000.qs2")
cc_qian <- qs_read("objects/cc_qian_20000.qs2")
```

```{r}
#| label: run-decoupler-pipeline
#| eval: false
dir.create("data/decoupler", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create("results/tf_activity", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

collectri_file <- "data/decoupler/collectri.csv"
if (!file.exists(collectri_file)) {
  collectri_db <- get_collectri(organism = "human", split_complexes = FALSE)
  write.csv(collectri_db, collectri_file, row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  collectri_db <- read.csv(collectri_file)
}

cohort_list <- list(pal = seu_pal, wu = seu_wu, qian = seu_qian)

for (cohort_name in names(cohort_list)) {
  message(sprintf("Processing cohort: %s", cohort_name))
  seu <- cohort_list[[cohort_name]]
  Idents(seu) <- "harmonized_label"
  available <- levels(Idents(seu))

  for (i in 1:nrow(candidate_registry)) {
    message(sprintf(" - Processing axis: %s", candidate_registry$axis_id[i]))
    row <- candidate_registry[i, ]
    axis_id <- row$axis_id
    l <- row$ligand
    r <- row$receptor
    sender <- row$sender_celltype
    receiver <- row$receiver_celltype

    if (!(sender %in% available) || !(receiver %in% available)) next

    seu_rec <- subset(seu, harmonized_label == receiver)
    counts <- GetAssayData(seu_rec, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
    samples <- as.factor(seu_rec$sample_id)

    design <- model.matrix(~ 0 + samples)
    colnames(design) <- levels(samples)
    pb_counts <- as.matrix(counts %*% design)
    pb_logcpm <- log2(t(t(pb_counts) / colSums(pb_counts)) * 1e6 + 1)

    activities <- run_wmean(
      mat = pb_logcpm,
      net = collectri_db,
      .source = "source",
      .target = "target",
      .mor = "weight",
      times = 100,
      minsize = 5
    ) %>% filter(statistic == "norm_wmean")

    seu_send <- subset(seu, harmonized_label == sender)
    counts_send <- GetAssayData(seu_send, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
    if (!(l %in% rownames(counts_send))) next

    ligand_counts <- counts_send[l, ]
    samples_send <- as.factor(seu_send$sample_id)
    ligand_pb <- tapply(ligand_counts, samples_send, sum)
    libsizes_send <- tapply(colSums(counts_send), samples_send, sum)
    ligand_logcpm <- log2((ligand_pb / libsizes_send) * 1e6 + 1)

    if (r %in% rownames(pb_counts)) {
      receptor_pb <- pb_counts[r, ]
      receptor_logcpm <- log2((receptor_pb / colSums(pb_counts)) * 1e6 + 1)
    } else {
      receptor_logcpm <- rep(0, ncol(pb_counts))
      names(receptor_logcpm) <- colnames(pb_counts)
    }

    common_samples <- intersect(names(ligand_logcpm), colnames(pb_logcpm))
    if (length(common_samples) < 5) next

    ligand_aligned <- ligand_logcpm[common_samples]
    receptor_aligned <- receptor_logcpm[common_samples]

    act_wide <- activities %>%
      filter(condition %in% common_samples) %>%
      dplyr::select(source, condition, score) %>%
      pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = score) %>%
      arrange(match(condition, common_samples))

    tf_names <- setdiff(colnames(act_wide), "condition")
    cor_df <- data.frame(TF = character(), Correlation = numeric(), PValue = numeric(), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

    for (tf in tf_names) {
      tf_scores <- act_wide[[tf]]
      sd_val <- sd(tf_scores, na.rm = TRUE)
      if (is.na(sd_val) || sd_val == 0) next

      # Multiple regression adjusting for receptor availability
      fit <- tryCatch(lm(tf_scores ~ ligand_aligned + receptor_aligned), error = function(e) NULL)
      if (is.null(fit)) next
      fit_summary <- summary(fit)
      coef_mat <- fit_summary$coefficients

      if ("ligand_aligned" %in% rownames(coef_mat)) {
        r_val <- cor(tf_scores, ligand_aligned, use = "complete.obs")
        pval <- coef_mat["ligand_aligned", "Pr(>|t|)"]
        if (!is.na(r_val) && !is.na(pval)) {
          cor_df <- rbind(cor_df, data.frame(
            TF = tf,
            Correlation = r_val,
            PValue = pval,
            stringsAsFactors = FALSE
          ))
        }
      }
    }

    if (nrow(cor_df) > 0) {
      cor_df$FDR <- p.adjust(cor_df$PValue, method = "BH")
      cor_df <- cor_df %>% arrange(FDR, desc(abs(Correlation)))
    }

    write.csv(cor_df, sprintf("results/tf_activity/tf_activity_%s_%s.csv", axis_id, cohort_name), row.names = FALSE)
  }
}
```

Across cohorts, per-TF correlations are combined with Fisher's z transformation, and a TF is called concordant if the sign of its correlation is the same in every cohort in which it was tested (TFs seen in a single cohort are dropped). We write the integrated tables and draw the strongest TFs per axis (@fig-tf-integrated-cxcl12_cxcr4 and the other tabs of the set). It also draws the per-cohort correlations (@fig-tf-cohort-cxcl12_cxcr4 and the other tabs of the set).

```{r}
#| label: decoupler-per-cohort-plots
#| eval: true
dir.create("results/tf_activity/plots", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
tf_cohort_plots <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(candidate_registry))) {
  axis <- candidate_registry$axis_id[i]
  plots <- list()
  for (ch in c("pal", "wu", "qian")) {
    f <- sprintf("results/tf_activity/tf_activity_%s_%s.csv", axis, ch)
    if (!file.exists(f)) next
    df <- read.csv(f)
    if (nrow(df) == 0) next
    p <- ggplot(head(df, 20), aes(x = reorder(TF, Correlation), y = Correlation, fill = Correlation)) +
      geom_col(width = 0.75, alpha = 0.9) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.6) +
      coord_flip() +
      scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "grey95", high = "#B2182B", midpoint = 0, guide = "none") +
      labs(x = NULL, y = "Correlation (r)") +
      theme_publication() +
      theme(
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
      )
    plots[[ch]] <- p
    ggsave(sprintf("results/tf_activity/plots/tf_%s_%s.png", axis, ch), plot = p, width = 4.5, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
  }
  tf_cohort_plots[[axis]] <- wrap_plots(plots, ncol = 3) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: decoupler-cross-cohort-integration

dir.create("results/tf_activity/plots", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create("results/tf_activity/tables", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

cohorts <- c("pal", "wu", "qian")
tf_integrated_plots <- list()

for (i in seq_len(nrow(candidate_registry))) {
  row <- candidate_registry[i, ]
  axis <- row$axis_id
  l <- row$ligand
  r <- row$receptor
  sender <- row$sender_celltype
  receiver <- row$receiver_celltype

  dfs <- list()
  for (ch in cohorts) {
    f <- sprintf("results/tf_activity/tf_activity_%s_%s.csv", axis, ch)
    if (file.exists(f)) {
      d <- read.csv(f)
      d$Correlation <- pmin(pmax(d$Correlation, -0.999), 0.999)
        d$Cohort <- ch
        dfs[[ch]] <- d
    }
  }

  if (length(dfs) == 0) next
  all_tfs <- bind_rows(dfs)

  integrated_tfs <- all_tfs %>%
    group_by(TF) %>%
    summarise(
      CohortCount = n(),
      # Fisher z before averaging the correlations
      MeanCorrelation = tanh(mean(atanh(Correlation), na.rm = TRUE)),
      Concordance = ifelse(all(Correlation > 0) || all(Correlation < 0), "Concordant", "Discordant"),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    # Keep only TFs tested in at least two cohorts
    filter(CohortCount > 1) %>%
    # Sort by concordance, then cohort count, then correlation strength
    arrange(desc(Concordance == "Concordant"), desc(CohortCount), desc(abs(MeanCorrelation)))

  if(nrow(integrated_tfs) == 0) next

  top_tfs <- head(integrated_tfs, 15)

  p_tf <- ggplot(top_tfs, aes(x = reorder(TF, MeanCorrelation), y = MeanCorrelation, fill = MeanCorrelation)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.75, alpha = 0.9) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.6) +
    coord_flip() +
    scale_fill_gradient2(
      low = "#2166AC", mid = "grey95", high = "#B2182B",
      midpoint = 0, guide = "none"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    labs(
      x = NULL,
      y = "Mean Pearson r (Fisher Z-adjusted)"
    ) +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold", color = "black"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"),
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", color = "black"),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey85", linewidth = 0.4),
      plot.margin = margin(t = 10, r = 15, b = 15, l = 15)
    )
  tf_integrated_plots[[axis]] <- p_tf

  ggsave(sprintf("results/tf_activity/plots/tf_integrated_%s.png", axis), plot = p_tf, width = 4.6, height = 5.0, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
  ggsave(sprintf("figures/tf_integrated_%s.png", axis), plot = p_tf, width = 4.6, height = 5.0, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
  ggsave(sprintf("figures/tf_integrated_mean_%s.png", axis), plot = p_tf, width = 4.6, height = 5.0, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

  write.csv(head(integrated_tfs, 8), sprintf("results/tf_activity/tables/tf_table_%s.csv", axis), row.names = FALSE)
}
```

These TF analyses are descriptive. After correction for the roughly 765 TFs tested in each run, the number of TFs with FDR below 0.05 is small, and no TF passes in more than one cohort for any axis (the table in the next section lists the counts per axis and cohort). The "cohort-concordant" TFs in the figures are concordant in sign, and should be read as candidate regulators and not as established master regulators.

## Per-cohort pseudobulk differential expression

For each axis and cohort we compare the pseudobulk profiles of receiver cells between ligand-high and ligand-low samples with edgeR's quasi-likelihood framework (genes filtered with `filterByExpr`, TMM normalization). The groups have 7 to 16 samples per group in Pal, 10 to 13 in Wu and 4 to 7 in Qian, so power is limited, especially in Qian. Differentially expressed genes are those with FDR below 0.05. When fewer than 10 genes pass, we fall back to nominal p below 0.05, and we flag these runs. The differentially expressed genes of each run then go through NicheNet. Candidate targets are ranked by the composite regulatory potential, the product of NicheNet's prior potential of the ligand for the gene and one plus the absolute log fold change, and we also record the activity rank of the axis ligand among all potential ligands. A contrast-level TF activity is computed by decoupleR's univariate linear model on the differential expression statistic.

```{r}
#| label: rev-pseudobulk-run
#| eval: false
suppressMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(qs2)
  library(Matrix)
  library(Seurat)
  library(edgeR)
  library(nichenetr)
  library(decoupleR)
})

set.seed(42)
ligand_target_matrix <- readRDS("data/nichenet/ligand_target_matrix_nsga2r_final.rds")
lr_network <- readRDS("data/nichenet/lr_network_human_21122021.rds")
collectri_db <- read.csv("data/decoupler/collectri.csv")


out_path <- "objects/revision/pseudobulk_nichenet.qs2"
results <- if (file.exists(out_path)) qs_read(out_path) else list()

for (cohort in c("pal", "wu", "qian")) {
  if (all(paste(cohort, candidate_registry$axis_id, sep = "_") %in% names(results))) next
  message(sprintf("[%s] %s: loading", Sys.time(), cohort))
  seu <- qs_read(sprintf("objects/seu_%s_harmonized_20000.qs2", cohort))
  counts <- GetAssayData(seu, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
  meta <- seu@meta.data
  rm(seu)
  gc()

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(candidate_registry))) {
    row <- candidate_registry[i, ]
    key <- paste(cohort, row$axis_id, sep = "_")
    send_idx <- which(meta$harmonized_label == row$sender_celltype)
    rec_idx <- which(meta$harmonized_label == row$receiver_celltype)
    rec_genes <- strsplit(row$receptor, "_")[[1]]
    rec_pct <- max(sapply(intersect(rec_genes, rownames(counts)), function(g) mean(counts[g, rec_idx] > 0)))
    if (length(send_idx) == 0 || length(rec_idx) == 0 || rec_pct < 0.02) {
      results[[key]] <- list(cohort = cohort, axis_id = row$axis_id, status = "receptor below 2% or cell type absent")
      next
    }

    # Stratification: median split of the per-sample ligand detection rate in sender cells
    send_tab <- data.frame(sample = meta$sample_id[send_idx], det = as.numeric(counts[row$ligand, send_idx] > 0)) %>%
      group_by(sample) %>%
      summarise(n_sender = n(), det_rate = mean(det), .groups = "drop") %>%
      filter(n_sender >= 10)
    send_tab$ligand_group <- ifelse(send_tab$det_rate >= median(send_tab$det_rate), "High", "Low")

    rec_n <- table(meta$sample_id[rec_idx])
    samples <- intersect(names(rec_n)[rec_n >= 10], send_tab$sample)
    send_tab <- send_tab %>% filter(sample %in% samples)
    group <- factor(send_tab$ligand_group, levels = c("Low", "High"))
    if (min(table(group)) < 2) {
      results[[key]] <- list(cohort = cohort, axis_id = row$axis_id, status = "fewer than 2 samples per group", send_tab = send_tab)
      next
    }

    rec_cells <- rec_idx[meta$sample_id[rec_idx] %in% samples]
    sample_factor <- factor(meta$sample_id[rec_cells], levels = send_tab$sample)
    pb <- as.matrix(counts[, rec_cells] %*% sparse.model.matrix(~ 0 + sample_factor))
    colnames(pb) <- levels(sample_factor)

    y <- DGEList(pb, group = group)
    y <- y[filterByExpr(y, group = group), , keep.lib.sizes = FALSE]
    y <- calcNormFactors(y)
    design <- model.matrix(~ group)
    y <- estimateDisp(y, design)
    fit <- glmQLFit(y, design, robust = TRUE)
    de <- topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, coef = 2), n = Inf)$table
    de$gene <- rownames(de)

    n_fdr <- sum(de$FDR < 0.05)
    fallback <- n_fdr < 10
    deg <- if (fallback) de %>% filter(PValue < 0.05) else de %>% filter(FDR < 0.05)

    # Background: genes detected in >= 5% of receiver cells and present in the prior
    pct_rec <- Matrix::rowMeans(counts[, rec_idx] > 0)
    background <- intersect(names(pct_rec)[pct_rec >= 0.05], rownames(ligand_target_matrix))
    goi <- intersect(deg$gene, background)

    targets <- data.frame(Gene = goi, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
      left_join(deg %>% select(Gene = gene, logFC, PValue, FDR), by = "Gene") %>%
      mutate(PriorPotential = ligand_target_matrix[Gene, row$ligand],
             RegulatoryPotential = PriorPotential * (1 + abs(logFC))) %>%
      arrange(desc(RegulatoryPotential))

    expressed_receptors <- names(pct_rec)[pct_rec >= 0.05]
    potential_ligands <- intersect(unique(lr_network$from[lr_network$to %in% expressed_receptors]), colnames(ligand_target_matrix))
    potential_ligands <- union(potential_ligands, row$ligand)
    activity <- if (length(goi) >= 5) {
      predict_ligand_activities(geneset = goi, background_expressed_genes = background,
                                ligand_target_matrix = ligand_target_matrix, potential_ligands = potential_ligands) %>%
        arrange(desc(aupr_corrected)) %>%
        mutate(rank = row_number())
    } else {
      NULL
    }

    stat_mat <- matrix(sign(de$logFC) * sqrt(de$F), ncol = 1, dimnames = list(de$gene, "contrast"))
    tf <- run_ulm(mat = stat_mat, net = collectri_db, .source = "source", .target = "target", .mor = "weight", minsize = 5) %>%
      mutate(FDR = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"))

    results[[key]] <- list(
      cohort = cohort, axis_id = row$axis_id, status = "ok",
      send_tab = send_tab, n_high = sum(group == "High"), n_low = sum(group == "Low"),
      n_genes_tested = nrow(de), n_fdr = n_fdr, fallback = fallback, n_deg_used = nrow(deg),
      de = de, targets = targets, activity = activity, n_potential_ligands = length(potential_ligands), tf = tf
    )
    message(sprintf("[%s] %s: %d vs %d samples, %d genes FDR<0.05, %d targets", Sys.time(), key,
                    sum(group == "High"), sum(group == "Low"), n_fdr, nrow(targets)))
    qs_save(results, out_path)
  }
  rm(counts, meta)
  gc()
}
qs_save(results, out_path)
message("Pseudobulk / NicheNet pipeline finished")
```


At the level of samples, most contrasts are underpowered: `r sum(pb_summary$degs_fdr05 < 10, na.rm = TRUE)` of the `r sum(pb_summary$status == "ok")` axis-cohort runs yield fewer than 10 genes at FDR below 0.05 and use the nominal fallback. The exceptions are CXCL12-CXCR4 in Pal (`r pb_summary$degs_fdr05[pb_summary$axis_id == "cxcl12_cxcr4" & pb_summary$cohort == "pal"]` genes) and FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1 in Qian (`r pb_summary$degs_fdr05[pb_summary$axis_id == "fn1_itga5_itgb1" & pb_summary$cohort == "qian"]` genes), which is the smallest cohort. Cell-level gene lists therefore overstate the evidence, because cells from the same sample are not independent. The ligand activity of FN1 sits above the median of potential ligands in all three cohorts (59th to 76th percentile), without being top-ranked, and CCL5 ranks at the 29th, 80th and 91st percentiles. No TF reaches FDR below 0.05 in more than one cohort for any axis, with either the regression or the contrast-level activity.

## Pooling the cohorts

Because the per-cohort contrasts are small, we pooled the samples of the three cohorts. Ligand groups are defined within each cohort as above, so the stratification is unchanged. The model is `~ cohort + ligand_group`, which absorbs differences between cohorts and tests the ligand-group coefficient on 48 to 69 samples per axis. Genes are restricted to those measured in all three cohorts, and the NicheNet target ranking, ligand activity and contrast-level TF activity are computed as before on the genes at FDR below 0.05.

```{r}
#| label: rev-pseudobulk-pooled-run
#| eval: false
suppressMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(qs2)
  library(Matrix)
  library(Seurat)
  library(edgeR)
  library(nichenetr)
  library(decoupleR)
})

set.seed(42)
ligand_target_matrix <- readRDS("data/nichenet/ligand_target_matrix_nsga2r_final.rds")
lr_network <- readRDS("data/nichenet/lr_network_human_21122021.rds")
collectri_db <- read.csv("data/decoupler/collectri.csv")


# Per cohort: receiver pseudobulks, per-sample ligand groups and receiver detection counts per gene
inputs_path <- "objects/revision/pseudobulk_pooled_inputs.qs2"
if (file.exists(inputs_path)) {
  inputs <- qs_read(inputs_path)
} else {
  inputs <- list()
  for (cohort in c("pal", "wu", "qian")) {
    message(sprintf("[%s] %s: loading", Sys.time(), cohort))
    seu <- qs_read(sprintf("objects/seu_%s_harmonized_20000.qs2", cohort))
    counts <- GetAssayData(seu, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
    meta <- seu@meta.data
    rm(seu)
    gc()
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(candidate_registry))) {
      row <- candidate_registry[i, ]
      send_idx <- which(meta$harmonized_label == row$sender_celltype)
      rec_idx <- which(meta$harmonized_label == row$receiver_celltype)
      if (length(send_idx) == 0 || length(rec_idx) == 0) next
      send_tab <- data.frame(sample = meta$sample_id[send_idx], det = as.numeric(counts[row$ligand, send_idx] > 0)) %>%
        group_by(sample) %>%
        summarise(n_sender = n(), det_rate = mean(det), .groups = "drop") %>%
        filter(n_sender >= 10)
      send_tab$ligand_group <- ifelse(send_tab$det_rate >= median(send_tab$det_rate), "High", "Low")
      rec_n <- table(meta$sample_id[rec_idx])
      samples <- intersect(names(rec_n)[rec_n >= 10], send_tab$sample)
      send_tab <- send_tab %>% filter(sample %in% samples) %>% mutate(cohort = cohort)
      rec_cells <- rec_idx[meta$sample_id[rec_idx] %in% samples]
      sample_factor <- factor(meta$sample_id[rec_cells], levels = send_tab$sample)
      pb <- as.matrix(counts[, rec_cells] %*% sparse.model.matrix(~ 0 + sample_factor))
      colnames(pb) <- paste(cohort, levels(sample_factor), sep = "__")
      inputs[[paste(cohort, row$axis_id, sep = "_")]] <- list(
        pb = pb, send_tab = send_tab,
        detected = Matrix::rowSums(counts[, rec_idx] > 0), n_receiver = length(rec_idx)
      )
    }
    rm(counts, meta)
    gc()
  }
  qs_save(inputs, inputs_path)
}

results <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(candidate_registry))) {
  row <- candidate_registry[i, ]
  parts <- inputs[paste(c("pal", "wu", "qian"), row$axis_id, sep = "_")]
  parts <- parts[!vapply(parts, is.null, logical(1))]
  genes <- Reduce(intersect, lapply(parts, function(x) rownames(x$pb)))
  pb <- do.call(cbind, lapply(parts, function(x) x$pb[genes, , drop = FALSE]))
  send_tab <- bind_rows(lapply(parts, `[[`, "send_tab"))
  cohort <- factor(send_tab$cohort)
  group <- factor(send_tab$ligand_group, levels = c("Low", "High"))

  y <- DGEList(pb, group = group)
  y <- y[filterByExpr(y, group = group), , keep.lib.sizes = FALSE]
  y <- calcNormFactors(y)
  design <- model.matrix(~ cohort + group)
  y <- estimateDisp(y, design)
  fit <- glmQLFit(y, design, robust = TRUE)
  de <- topTags(glmQLFTest(fit, coef = "groupHigh"), n = Inf)$table
  de$gene <- rownames(de)
  deg <- de %>% filter(FDR < 0.05)

  pct_rec <- Reduce(`+`, lapply(parts, function(x) x$detected[genes])) / sum(vapply(parts, `[[`, numeric(1), "n_receiver"))
  background <- intersect(names(pct_rec)[pct_rec >= 0.05], rownames(ligand_target_matrix))
  goi <- intersect(deg$gene, background)
  targets <- data.frame(Gene = goi, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    left_join(deg %>% select(Gene = gene, logFC, PValue, FDR), by = "Gene") %>%
    mutate(PriorPotential = ligand_target_matrix[Gene, row$ligand], RegulatoryPotential = PriorPotential * (1 + abs(logFC))) %>%
    arrange(desc(RegulatoryPotential))
  expressed_receptors <- names(pct_rec)[pct_rec >= 0.05]
  potential_ligands <- union(intersect(unique(lr_network$from[lr_network$to %in% expressed_receptors]), colnames(ligand_target_matrix)), row$ligand)
  activity <- if (length(goi) >= 5) {
    predict_ligand_activities(geneset = goi, background_expressed_genes = background,
                              ligand_target_matrix = ligand_target_matrix, potential_ligands = potential_ligands) %>%
      arrange(desc(aupr_corrected)) %>%
      mutate(rank = row_number())
  } else {
    NULL
  }
  stat_mat <- matrix(sign(de$logFC) * sqrt(de$F), ncol = 1, dimnames = list(de$gene, "contrast"))
  tf <- run_ulm(mat = stat_mat, net = collectri_db, .source = "source", .target = "target", .mor = "weight", minsize = 5) %>%
    mutate(FDR = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"))

  results[[row$axis_id]] <- list(
    axis_id = row$axis_id, n_samples = ncol(pb), n_high = sum(group == "High"), n_low = sum(group == "Low"),
    samples_by_cohort = table(send_tab$cohort, send_tab$ligand_group), n_genes_tested = nrow(de), n_fdr = nrow(deg),
    de = de, targets = targets, activity = activity, n_potential_ligands = length(potential_ligands), tf = tf
  )
  message(sprintf("[%s] %s: %d samples (%d high / %d low), %d genes tested, %d FDR<0.05, %d NicheNet targets",
                  Sys.time(), row$axis_id, ncol(pb), sum(group == "High"), sum(group == "Low"), nrow(de), nrow(deg), nrow(targets)))
}
qs_save(results, "objects/revision/pseudobulk_pooled.qs2")
message("Pooled pseudobulk finished")
```

```{r}

```

FN1-high endothelium shows two coordinated changes.

- **Up:** a basement-membrane and angiogenic remodeling program: NID1, LAMA4, COL4A1, MMP2 and SPARC, the guidance and sprouting receptors NRP2, UNC5B, EFNB2, PODXL and CALCRL, the TGF-β target PMEPA1, and the α5 integrin subunit ITGA5 itself (log fold change `r sprintf("%.2f", fn1_pooled$de$logFC[fn1_pooled$de$gene == "ITGA5"])`, FDR `r sprintf("%.3f", fn1_pooled$de$FDR[fn1_pooled$de$gene == "ITGA5"])`).
- **Down:** the immediate-early genes EGR1, JUNB and BTG2, and the endothelial MHC-II program. CIITA and the RFX complex are the strongest TF changes, together with HLA-DMA.

There is no NF-κB signal: NFKBIA changes by `r sprintf("%.2f", fn1_pooled$de$logFC[fn1_pooled$de$gene == "NFKBIA"])` log2 units (FDR `r sprintf("%.2f", fn1_pooled$de$FDR[fn1_pooled$de$gene == "NFKBIA"])`). The immediate-early genes that appeared among the per-cohort top targets were ranked by absolute fold change on nominal gene lists, which hid their direction. In the pooled analysis they go down. In the NicheNet ligand-activity analysis, FN1 ranks `r pooled_summary$ligand_activity_rank[pooled_summary$axis_id == "fn1_itga5_itgb1"]` of `r pooled_summary$ligand_activity_n[pooled_summary$axis_id == "fn1_itga5_itgb1"]` potential ligands, at percentile `r round(pooled_summary$ligand_activity_percentile[pooled_summary$axis_id == "fn1_itga5_itgb1"])`, behind collagens, MMP14, TGF-β and VEGFA. That points to a fibroblast-derived matrix niche acting on the endothelium as a whole, of which FN1 is one component. Some of the up-regulated genes are usually fibroblast or mural transcripts (THY1, MMP14 and COL6A2), and NID1, SPARC, MMP2 and COL4A1 are also expressed by fibroblasts. In stroma-rich FN1-high tumors they may reflect ambient RNA or contaminating cells in the endothelial pseudobulk, so we rest the interpretation on the endothelial-enriched genes NRP2, UNC5B, EFNB2, PODXL and CALCRL and on the CIITA/MHC-II program.

Our reading is that FN1-high microenvironments are associated with an endothelial program of basement-membrane remodeling and angiogenic sprouting, together with a reduced endothelial MHC-II antigen-presentation program. The second element was not anticipated, and it links to the finding of the section "Tumor microenvironment deconvolution" that FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1 is the only axis negatively correlated with CD8+ T cells. We treat that link as a hypothesis.

Among the other axes:

- CCL5-ACKR1 and MDK-LRP1 have no gene at FDR below 0.05 even with about 67 samples.
- The 34 CXCL12-CXCR4 genes in T cells are dominated by luminal epithelial transcripts (TFF3, TRPS1, SLC39A6, STARD10 and GSTM3), which suggests ambient RNA or contamination in stroma-rich samples more than a T-cell response. We do not interpret them.
- The two APP-CD74 genes are immunoglobulin transcripts.

## ACKR1 as a non-signaling reference axis

ACKR1 is an atypical chemokine receptor. It transports chemokines across endothelial cells and presents them on the luminal surface, and it lacks the intracellular domain for G-protein signaling. A transcriptional program downstream of CCL5-ACKR1 engagement is therefore not expected. The pooled analysis has no gene at FDR below 0.05, although nine TF activities pass, all higher in CCL5-high samples and pointing to an interferon and MHC class II state (CIITA, IRF1 and STAT1, among others). We use CCL5-ACKR1 as a reference axis whose results describe the neighborhood of T-cell-rich venules and not a signaling cascade. The nominal, ligand-associated programs in the per-cohort analyses are of an interferon and inflammatory endothelial state (TNFSF10, IFITM1 and IFI16 in Pal, IL6, BIRC3 and IFIT3 in Wu, STAT1, MX1 and ISG15 in Qian), which co-occurs with CCL5-producing T cells, in line with T-cell-infiltrated, inflamed vasculature. We describe these as ligand-associated receiver programs, and we read the lack of a pooled signal as consistent with an axis that moves cells and chemokines and does not alter endothelial transcription.

Power limits all of these results. Qian has 14 samples, with 4 to 7 per group, and Wu 22 to 25 usable samples, so a null result here is weak evidence of absence.

## Pathway scores and survival

The programs above can also be scored and tested against survival, which is done in the section "Clinical associations".


# Tumor vs normal tissue

Do the axes also describe normal breast tissue? We address this in bulk with patient-matched TCGA samples, and at the single-cell level with normal breast samples from the Pal cohort.

## TCGA tumors against adjacent normal tissue

The TCGA expression on disk is the PanCancer Atlas release (`brca_tcga_pan_can_atlas_2018`, batch-normalized RSEM). Its adjacent-normal profiles come from the same release, so tumor and normal samples are normalized identically: library-size scaling to counts per million, then log2(CPM + 1). The comparison is paired by patient (114 tumor-normal pairs) and uses a Wilcoxon signed-rank test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction across the genes and axis scores.

```{r}
#| label: rev-tcga-tumour-normal
#| eval: true
read_rsem_cpm <- function(path) {
  raw <- fread(path)
  raw <- raw[Hugo_Symbol != "" & !is.na(Hugo_Symbol)]
  raw <- raw[!duplicated(Hugo_Symbol)]
  m <- as.matrix(raw[, -c("Hugo_Symbol", "Entrez_Gene_Id"), with = FALSE])
  rownames(m) <- raw$Hugo_Symbol
  m <- apply(m, 2, function(x) x / sum(x, na.rm = TRUE) * 1e6)
  rownames(m)[rownames(m) == "DARC"] <- "ACKR1"
  rownames(m)[rownames(m) == "IL8"] <- "CXCL8"
  log2(m + 1)
}
tn_genes <- c("CCL5", "ACKR1", "FN1", "ITGA5", "ITGB1", "CXCL12", "CXCR4", "MDK", "LRP1", "APP", "CD74")
tcga_normal_log <- read_rsem_cpm("data/ext/brca_tcga/normals/data_mrna_seq_v2_rsem_normal_samples.txt")[tn_genes, ]
tcga_tumour_log <- read_rsem_cpm("data/ext/brca_tcga/data_mrna_seq_v2_rsem.txt")[tn_genes, ]

pairs <- tibble::tibble(normal = colnames(tcga_normal_log), patient = substr(normal, 1, 12)) %>%
  inner_join(tibble::tibble(tumour = colnames(tcga_tumour_log), patient = substr(tumour, 1, 12)), by = "patient") %>%
  distinct(patient, .keep_all = TRUE)

feature_values <- function(m) {
  out <- as.data.frame(t(m))
  out$ITGA5_ITGB1 <- (out$ITGA5 + out$ITGB1) / 2
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(candidate_registry))) {
    out[[paste0("score_", candidate_registry$axis_id[i])]] <- (out[[candidate_registry$ligand[i]]] + out[[candidate_registry$receptor[i]]]) / 2
  }
  out
}
tum_feat <- feature_values(tcga_tumour_log[, pairs$tumour])
norm_feat <- feature_values(tcga_normal_log[, pairs$normal])

tn_res <- bind_rows(lapply(colnames(tum_feat), function(f) {
  d <- tum_feat[[f]] - norm_feat[[f]]
  wt <- wilcox.test(tum_feat[[f]], norm_feat[[f]], paired = TRUE)
  data.frame(feature = f, n_pairs = length(d), median_tumour = median(tum_feat[[f]]), median_normal = median(norm_feat[[f]]),
             median_log2fc = median(d), frac_tumour_higher = mean(d > 0), p = wt$p.value)
})) %>% mutate(q_bh = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"))
write_csv(tn_res, "results/revision/tcga_tumour_vs_adjacent_normal.csv")
knitr::kable(tn_res %>% rename_with(~ sub("tumour", "tumor", .x)), digits = 4, caption = sprintf("TCGA tumor vs patient-matched adjacent normal (%d pairs; paired Wilcoxon, BH)", nrow(pairs)))

```

FN1 is higher in the tumor in `r round(100 * tn_res$frac_tumour_higher[tn_res$feature == "FN1"])`% of pairs, by a median of `r sprintf("%.1f", tn_res$median_log2fc[tn_res$feature == "FN1"])` log2 units, and the FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1 score is higher by `r sprintf("%.2f", tn_res$median_log2fc[tn_res$feature == "score_fn1_itga5_itgb1"])`, with ITGA5 up and ITGB1 slightly down. ACKR1 goes the other way: it is lower in the tumor in `r round(100 * (1 - tn_res$frac_tumour_higher[tn_res$feature == "ACKR1"]))`% of pairs, by `r sprintf("%.1f", -tn_res$median_log2fc[tn_res$feature == "ACKR1"])` log2 units, while CCL5 is unchanged, so the CCL5-ACKR1 score is lower in tumors (`r sprintf("%.2f", tn_res$median_log2fc[tn_res$feature == "score_ccl5_ackr1"])`). CXCL12 and LRP1 are lower in tumors and CXCR4 and MDK are higher (@fig-tcga-tumor-normal). The lower ACKR1 expression in bulk tumors reflects, at least in part, the venule-rich architecture of normal breast tissue.

```{r}
#| label: fig-tcga-tumor-normal
#| eval: true
#| fig-cap: "Expression of the axis genes in TCGA tumors and patient-matched adjacent normal tissue. Lines connect the two samples of a patient."
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6
tn_plot_df <- bind_rows(
  tum_feat %>% mutate(patient = pairs$patient, tissue = "Tumour"),
  norm_feat %>% mutate(patient = pairs$patient, tissue = "Adjacent normal")
) %>%
  select(patient, tissue, all_of(c(tn_genes, "ITGA5_ITGB1"))) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(patient, tissue), names_to = "gene", values_to = "log2cpm") %>%
  mutate(tissue = factor(recode(tissue, Tumour = "Tumor"), levels = c("Adjacent normal", "Tumor")), gene = factor(gene, levels = c(tn_genes, "ITGA5_ITGB1")))
p_tn <- ggplot(tn_plot_df, aes(x = tissue, y = log2cpm)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = patient), color = "grey80", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = tissue), width = 0.5, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~gene, scales = "free_y", nrow = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Adjacent normal" = "#56B4E9", "Tumor" = "#E69F00")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "log2(CPM + 1)") +
  theme_publication() +
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
ggsave("results/revision/fig_tcga_tumour_vs_normal.png", p_tn, width = 12, height = 6, dpi = 300)
p_tn
```

## Normal breast tissue in the Pal cohort

The Pal cohort also profiled 13 normal breast samples ("Total" fraction) from women who had reduction mammoplasty, who are different women from the tumor patients. We process them with the tumor QC and integration settings, which gives 45,807 singlets from 63,970 raw cells. The Figshare annotation mapping covers tumors only, so we transfer labels from the annotated Pal tumor sketch with Seurat anchors. Reduction mammoplasty tissue contains no malignant cells, so we merge the "Cancer" predictions into `Normal_epithelial`. The cells are sketched to 20,000 and run through CellChat with the original settings. Because the donors are not the tumor patients, the comparison with tumors is unpaired.

```{r}
#| label: rev-normals-run
#| eval: false
suppressMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
  library(qs2)
  library(Matrix)
  library(Seurat)
  library(harmony)
  library(scDblFinder)
  library(SingleCellExperiment)
  library(CellChat)
})

set.seed(42)
raw_dir <- "data/raw/BCS010_normal"
dir.create(raw_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("objects/revision", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Normal "Total" (unsorted) samples only, matching the tumor selection on cell population = Total
tar_members <- untar("data/GSE161529_RAW.tar", list = TRUE)
normal_members <- tar_members[grepl("_N-.*-Total-(matrix|barcodes)", tar_members)]
if (!all(file.exists(file.path(raw_dir, normal_members)))) {
  untar("data/GSE161529_RAW.tar", files = normal_members, exdir = raw_dir)
}
file.copy("data/raw/BCS010/GSE161529_features.tsv.gz", raw_dir, overwrite = FALSE)
normal_gsm <- unique(sub("_.*", "", normal_members))
message(sprintf("Normal Total samples: %d", length(normal_gsm)))

filtered_path <- "objects/revision/seu_pal_normal_filtered.qs2"
if (file.exists(filtered_path)) {
  seu_norm <- qs_read(filtered_path)
} else {
  features <- read.table(file.path(raw_dir, "GSE161529_features.tsv.gz"), sep = "\t", header = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  norm_objects <- list()
  norm_stats <- list()
  for (gsm in normal_gsm) {
    files <- list.files(raw_dir, full.names = TRUE)
    mat <- readMM(files[grep(paste0("^", gsm, ".*matrix.mtx.gz$"), basename(files))])
    barcodes <- readLines(files[grep(paste0("^", gsm, ".*barcodes.tsv.gz$"), basename(files))])
    rownames(mat) <- make.unique(features$V2)
    colnames(mat) <- paste0(gsm, "_", barcodes)
    title <- sub("^GSM[0-9]+_", "", basename(files[grep(paste0("^", gsm, ".*matrix.mtx.gz$"), basename(files))]))

    seu <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = mat, project = gsm)
    seu$sample_id <- gsm
    seu$patient_id <- paste0("PalN_", sub("-Total.*", "", sub("^N-", "", title)))
    seu$cohort <- "Pal_normal"
    seu[["percent.mt"]] <- PercentageFeatureSet(seu, pattern = "^MT-")

    feat_lim <- get_mad_limits(seu$nFeature_RNA, nmads = 3)
    count_lim <- get_mad_limits(seu$nCount_RNA, nmads = 3)
    mt_lim <- get_mad_limits(seu$percent.mt, nmads = 3)
    feat_lower <- max(feat_lim$lower, 200)
    feat_upper <- feat_lim$upper
    count_upper <- count_lim$upper
    mt_upper <- min(max(mt_lim$upper, 5), 15)
    n_raw <- ncol(seu)

    seu_qc <- subset(
      seu,
      subset = nFeature_RNA >= feat_lower &
               nFeature_RNA <= feat_upper &
               nCount_RNA <= count_upper &
               percent.mt <= mt_upper
    )
    if (ncol(seu_qc) > 10) {
      sce <- as.SingleCellExperiment(seu_qc)
      sce <- scDblFinder(sce, BPPARAM = BiocParallel::MulticoreParam(workers = 16))
      seu_qc$doublet_class <- sce$scDblFinder.class
      seu_final <- subset(seu_qc, doublet_class == "singlet")
    } else {
      seu_final <- seu_qc
    }
    norm_stats[[gsm]] <- data.frame(sample = gsm, cells_raw = n_raw, cells_qc = ncol(seu_qc), cells_final = ncol(seu_final))
    norm_objects[[gsm]] <- seu_final
  }
  write_csv(bind_rows(norm_stats), "results/revision/pal_normal_qc_stats.csv")
  seu_norm <- merge(norm_objects[[1]], norm_objects[-1])
  seu_norm <- JoinLayers(seu_norm)
  qs_save(seu_norm, filtered_path)
}

integrated_path <- "objects/revision/seu_pal_normal_integrated.qs2"
if (file.exists(integrated_path)) {
  seu_norm <- qs_read(integrated_path)
} else {
  seu_norm <- NormalizeData(seu_norm)
  seu_norm <- FindVariableFeatures(seu_norm, nfeatures = 2000)
  seu_norm <- ScaleData(seu_norm)
  seu_norm <- RunPCA(seu_norm, npcs = 30)
  seu_norm <- RunHarmony(seu_norm, group.by.vars = "patient_id", max_iter = 10)
  seu_norm <- RunUMAP(seu_norm, reduction = "harmony", dims = 1:30, reduction.name = "umap_after")
  seu_norm <- FindNeighbors(seu_norm, reduction = "harmony", dims = 1:30)
  seu_norm <- FindClusters(seu_norm, resolution = 0.8)
  qs_save(seu_norm, integrated_path)
}

# The Figshare mappings cover tumors only, so labels are transferred from the annotated Pal tumor sketch
harmonized_path <- "objects/revision/seu_pal_normal_harmonized_20000.qs2"
if (file.exists(harmonized_path)) {
  seu_norm <- qs_read(harmonized_path)
} else {
  seu_ref <- qs_read("objects/seu_pal_harmonized_20000.qs2")
  seu_ref <- subset(seu_ref, cells = colnames(seu_ref[["sketch"]]))
  DefaultAssay(seu_ref) <- "sketch"
  seu_ref[["RNA"]] <- NULL
  seu_ref <- ScaleData(seu_ref, verbose = FALSE)
  seu_ref <- RunPCA(seu_ref, npcs = 30, verbose = FALSE)

  anchors <- FindTransferAnchors(reference = seu_ref, query = seu_norm, dims = 1:30, reference.reduction = "pca")
  pred <- TransferData(anchorset = anchors, refdata = seu_ref$harmonized_label, dims = 1:30)
  seu_norm$transfer_label <- pred[colnames(seu_norm), "predicted.id"]
  seu_norm$transfer_score <- pred[colnames(seu_norm), "prediction.score.max"]
  # Normal reduction mammoplasty tissue contains no malignant cells
  seu_norm$harmonized_label <- ifelse(seu_norm$transfer_label == "Cancer", "Normal_epithelial", seu_norm$transfer_label)
  rm(seu_ref)
  gc()

  seu_norm <- SketchData(object = seu_norm, ncells = min(ncol(seu_norm), 20000), method = "LeverageScore", sketched.assay = "sketch")
  DefaultAssay(seu_norm) <- "sketch"
  seu_norm <- NormalizeData(seu_norm)
  qs_save(seu_norm, harmonized_path)
}

markers <- c("EPCAM", "KRT18", "KRT19", "CD3D", "CD3E", "CD19", "MS4A1", "CD14", "LYZ", "COL1A1", "DCN", "PECAM1", "VWF", "ACTA2", "RGS5")
marker_expr <- AverageExpression(seu_norm, assays = "RNA", features = markers, group.by = "harmonized_label", layer = "data")$RNA
write.csv(round(as.matrix(marker_expr), 3), "results/revision/pal_normal_marker_expression.csv")
write_csv(as.data.frame(table(harmonized_label = seu_norm$harmonized_label, transfer_label = seu_norm$transfer_label)),
          "results/revision/pal_normal_label_counts.csv")

cc_path <- "objects/revision/cc_pal_normal_20000.qs2"
if (!file.exists(cc_path)) {
  seu_sub <- subset(seu_norm, cells = colnames(seu_norm[["sketch"]]))
  data_input <- GetAssayData(seu_sub, assay = "sketch", layer = "data")
  cellchat <- createCellChat(object = data_input, meta = seu_sub@meta.data, group.by = "harmonized_label")
  cellchat@DB <- CellChatDB.human
  cellchat <- subsetData(cellchat)
  cellchat <- identifyOverExpressedGenes(cellchat)
  cellchat <- identifyOverExpressedInteractions(cellchat)
  cellchat <- computeCommunProb(cellchat, raw.use = TRUE)
  cellchat <- filterCommunication(cellchat, min.cells = 10)
  cellchat <- computeCommunProbPathway(cellchat)
  cellchat <- aggregateNet(cellchat)
  qs_save(cellchat, cc_path)
}

# Sample-level co-expression: mean ligand in sender cells x mean receptor in receiver cells (all cells, >= 10 per type)
normal_axes <- tibble::tribble(
  ~axis_id, ~ligand, ~receptor, ~sender_celltype, ~receiver_celltype,
  "cxcl12_cxcr4", "CXCL12", "CXCR4", "Fibroblast", "T_cell",
  "ccl5_ackr1", "CCL5", "ACKR1", "T_cell", "Endothelial",
  "mdk_lrp1", "MDK", "LRP1", "Fibroblast", "Fibroblast",
  "fn1_itga5_itgb1", "FN1", "ITGA5_ITGB1", "Fibroblast", "Endothelial",
  "app_cd74", "APP", "CD74", "Endothelial", "B_cell",
  "app_cd74_myeloid", "APP", "CD74", "Endothelial", "Myeloid"
)

sample_scores <- function(seu, tissue) {
  expr <- GetAssayData(seu, assay = "RNA", layer = "data")
  meta <- seu@meta.data
  out <- list()
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(normal_axes))) {
    rec_genes <- strsplit(normal_axes$receptor[i], "_")[[1]]
    for (smp in unique(meta$sample_id)) {
      send_cells <- rownames(meta)[meta$sample_id == smp & meta$harmonized_label == normal_axes$sender_celltype[i]]
      rec_cells <- rownames(meta)[meta$sample_id == smp & meta$harmonized_label == normal_axes$receiver_celltype[i]]
      if (length(send_cells) < 10 || length(rec_cells) < 10) next
      lig_mean <- mean(expr[normal_axes$ligand[i], send_cells])
      rec_mean <- mean(sapply(rec_genes, function(g) mean(expr[g, rec_cells])))
      out[[length(out) + 1]] <- data.frame(
        axis_id = normal_axes$axis_id[i], tissue = tissue, sample_id = smp,
        n_sender = length(send_cells), n_receiver = length(rec_cells),
        ligand_mean = lig_mean, receptor_mean = rec_mean, coexpression = lig_mean * rec_mean
      )
    }
  }
  bind_rows(out)
}

DefaultAssay(seu_norm) <- "RNA"
scores_normal <- sample_scores(seu_norm, "Normal")
rm(seu_norm)
gc()
seu_tum <- qs_read("objects/seu_pal_harmonized_20000.qs2")
DefaultAssay(seu_tum) <- "RNA"
scores_tumour <- sample_scores(seu_tum, "Tumour")
qs_save(bind_rows(scores_normal, scores_tumour), "objects/revision/pal_normal_tumour_sample_scores.qs2")
message("Normal-tissue pipeline finished")
```

Normal breast has almost no B cells (40 cells in total), which affects the APP-CD74 axis, whose receiver in the registry is the B cell. For that axis we also report the version with myeloid receivers, which is the receiver of the APP-CD74 interaction in the consensus set. We first compare the CellChat communication probability of each axis in tumor and normal, and then a sample-level score of ligand-receptor co-expression: the mean ligand expression in sender cells times the mean receptor expression in receiver cells, in samples with at least 10 cells of each type, tested with a Wilcoxon test and corrected within each measure (@fig-pal-normal).

```{r}
#| label: rev-pal-normal-tumour
#| eval: true
cc_normal <- qs_read("objects/revision/cc_pal_normal_20000.qs2")
cc_tumour <- qs_read("objects/cc_pal_20000.qs2")
normal_qc <- read_csv("results/revision/pal_normal_qc_stats.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
knitr::kable(normal_qc %>% summarise(samples = n(), raw_cells = sum(cells_raw), post_qc = sum(cells_qc), singlets = sum(cells_final)),
             caption = "Pal normal-breast Total samples: QC attrition")
knitr::kable(read_csv("results/revision/pal_normal_label_counts.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>% filter(Freq > 0),
             caption = "Label transfer from the Pal tumor reference (all normal cells)")
knitr::kable(read.csv("results/revision/pal_normal_marker_expression.csv", check.names = FALSE), digits = 2,
             caption = "Canonical markers by transferred label (normal tissue)")

axis_pairs_cc <- bind_rows(
  candidate_registry %>% select(axis_id, ligand, receptor, sender = sender_celltype, receiver = receiver_celltype),
  candidate_registry %>% filter(axis_id == "app_cd74") %>% transmute(axis_id, ligand, receptor, sender = sender_celltype, receiver = "Myeloid")
) %>% mutate(interaction_name = paste(ligand, receptor, sep = "_"))

cc_axis_value <- function(cc, sender, receiver, lr) {
  dn <- dimnames(cc@net$prob)
  if (!(sender %in% dn[[1]] && receiver %in% dn[[2]] && lr %in% dn[[3]])) return(c(prob = 0, pval = NA_real_))
  c(prob = cc@net$prob[sender, receiver, lr], pval = cc@net$pval[sender, receiver, lr])
}
nt_cc <- axis_pairs_cc %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    prob_tumour = cc_axis_value(cc_tumour, sender, receiver, interaction_name)[["prob"]],
    pval_tumour = cc_axis_value(cc_tumour, sender, receiver, interaction_name)[["pval"]],
    prob_normal = cc_axis_value(cc_normal, sender, receiver, interaction_name)[["prob"]],
    pval_normal = cc_axis_value(cc_normal, sender, receiver, interaction_name)[["pval"]]
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(log2_ratio_tumour_normal = log2((prob_tumour + 1e-6) / (prob_normal + 1e-6)))
write_csv(nt_cc, "results/revision/pal_normal_vs_tumour_cellchat.csv")
knitr::kable(nt_cc %>% mutate(Axis = axis_labels[axis_id]) %>% select(Axis, sender, receiver, prob_tumour, pval_tumour, prob_normal, pval_normal, log2_ratio_tumour_normal) %>% rename_with(~ sub("tumour", "tumor", .x)),
             digits = 4, caption = "CellChat communication probability of each axis in Pal tumor vs Pal normal breast (same settings, 20,000-cell sketches)")

nt_scores <- qs_read("objects/revision/pal_normal_tumour_sample_scores.qs2")
nt_tests <- nt_scores %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(ligand_mean, receptor_mean, coexpression), names_to = "measure", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(axis_id, measure) %>%
  summarise(
    n_tumour = sum(tissue == "Tumour"), n_normal = sum(tissue == "Normal"),
    median_tumour = median(value[tissue == "Tumour"]), median_normal = median(value[tissue == "Normal"]),
    p = if (n_tumour >= 3 && n_normal >= 3) wilcox.test(value[tissue == "Tumour"], value[tissue == "Normal"])$p.value else NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(measure) %>%
  mutate(q_bh = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(log2_ratio = log2(median_tumour / median_normal))
write_csv(nt_tests, "results/revision/pal_normal_vs_tumour_sample_scores.csv")
nt_label <- c(axis_labels, app_cd74_myeloid = "APP-CD74 (to Myeloid)")
knitr::kable(nt_tests %>% mutate(Axis = nt_label[axis_id]) %>% select(Axis, measure, everything(), -axis_id) %>% rename_with(~ sub("tumour", "tumor", .x)), digits = 4,
             caption = "Sample-level sender ligand, receiver receptor and co-expression (ligand x receptor) in Pal tumors vs normal breast (Wilcoxon, BH within measure)")

```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Sample-level co-expression of the ligand and receptor of each axis in Pal normal breast and tumor samples. Each point is a sample; the score is the mean log-normalized ligand in sender cells times the mean receptor in receiver cells."
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5
p_nt <- nt_scores %>%
  mutate(Axis = factor(nt_label[axis_id], levels = nt_label), tissue = factor(recode(tissue, Tumour = "Tumor"), levels = c("Normal", "Tumor"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = tissue, y = coexpression, fill = tissue)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.8, width = 0.6) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 1.2, alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~Axis, scales = "free_y", nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Normal" = "#56B4E9", "Tumor" = "#E69F00")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Co-expression score") +
  theme_publication() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
ggsave("results/revision/fig_pal_normal_vs_tumour.png", p_nt, width = 14, height = 5, dpi = 300)
p_nt
```
