At the single-cell level, FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1 communication is `r round(nt_cc$prob_tumour[nt_cc$axis_id == "fn1_itga5_itgb1"] / nt_cc$prob_normal[nt_cc$axis_id == "fn1_itga5_itgb1"])`-fold higher in tumors than in normal breast (probability `r sprintf("%.3f", nt_cc$prob_tumour[nt_cc$axis_id == "fn1_itga5_itgb1"])` against `r sprintf("%.3f", nt_cc$prob_normal[nt_cc$axis_id == "fn1_itga5_itgb1"])`) and CCL5-ACKR1 is `r sprintf("%.1f", nt_cc$prob_tumour[nt_cc$axis_id == "ccl5_ackr1"] / nt_cc$prob_normal[nt_cc$axis_id == "ccl5_ackr1"])`-fold higher. MDK-LRP1 is detected only in tumors, and APP-CD74 toward myeloid cells is higher in tumors. CXCL12-CXCR4 differs little. At the sample level, the FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1 co-expression score is higher in tumors by `r sprintf("%.2f", nt_tests$log2_ratio[nt_tests$axis_id == "fn1_itga5_itgb1" & nt_tests$measure == "coexpression"])` log2 units (q = `r sg(nt_tests$q_bh[nt_tests$axis_id == "fn1_itga5_itgb1" & nt_tests$measure == "coexpression"], 2)`), and the difference comes from fibroblast FN1, while endothelial ITGA5 and ITGB1 are unchanged. For CCL5-ACKR1 the score is higher by `r sprintf("%.2f", nt_tests$log2_ratio[nt_tests$axis_id == "ccl5_ackr1" & nt_tests$measure == "coexpression"])` log2 units (q = `r sg(nt_tests$q_bh[nt_tests$axis_id == "ccl5_ackr1" & nt_tests$measure == "coexpression"], 2)`), driven by T-cell CCL5, with per-cell ACKR1 in endothelial cells preserved.

FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1 is higher in breast cancer at both levels, and fibroblast fibronectin drives the increase. CCL5-ACKR1 communication is higher in tumors in single cells, driven by T cells, while ACKR1 is lower in bulk tumors compared with the venule-rich normal breast. A reading that fits both is that tumors which keep the ACKR1-positive venular niche, and T cells that deliver CCL5 to it, fare better, which is the protective reading of the survival results below. The caveats are that Wu and Qian have no normal samples, the Pal normal donors are unpaired with the tumor patients, and the TCGA "normal" tissue is tumor-adjacent.

# Spatial co-localization

Single-cell inference says which cell types could talk to each other. It does not say whether they are neighbors. We use spatial transcriptomics to ask whether the senders and receivers of each axis sit next to each other in tissue, and whether the ligand and receptor are co-expressed where they do. Co-localization supports but does not prove ligand-receptor engagement, because Visium spots hold several cells and a ligand and a receptor can be expressed near each other without binding.

## Visium sections from Wu et al.

We use the six Visium sections of Wu et al. (1142243F, 1160920F, CID4290, CID4465, CID44971 and CID4535). Four of them (CID4290, CID4465, CID44971 and CID4535) come from patients who are also in the Wu single-cell cohort, so they corroborate the discovery data but do not form an independent test. The FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1 axis is the primary hypothesis, CCL5-ACKR1 is the key secondary hypothesis, and the three remaining axes are exploratory.

### Data and spot quality control

In-tissue spots of the filtered count matrices are kept, apart from spots the pathologist annotated "Artefact" and spots with fewer than 500 UMIs or 250 detected genes. Expression is log-normalized per section (`LogNormalize`, scale factor 10,000), and the ITGA5_ITGB1 receptor is the mean of the log-normalized ITGA5 and ITGB1 values, matching the bulk definition.

```{r}
#| label: rev-spatial-data
#| eval: true
library(Matrix)

spatial_dir <- "data/spatial/wu2021_visium"
spatial_obj_dir <- "objects/revision/spatial"
spatial_res_dir <- "results/revision/spatial"
dir.create(spatial_obj_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(spatial_res_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

section_ids <- c("1142243F", "1160920F", "CID4290", "CID4465", "CID44971", "CID4535")
wu_sc_samples <- list.dirs("data/raw/BCS014", full.names = FALSE, recursive = FALSE)
sections_path <- file.path(spatial_obj_dir, "visium_sections.qs2")

if (file.exists(sections_path)) {
  visium <- qs_read(sections_path)
} else {
  visium <- lapply(setNames(section_ids, section_ids), function(sid) {
    mdir <- file.path(spatial_dir, "filtered_count_matrices", paste0(sid, "_filtered_count_matrix"))
    counts <- as(readMM(file.path(mdir, "matrix.mtx.gz")), "CsparseMatrix")
    rownames(counts) <- make.unique(readLines(file.path(mdir, "features.tsv.gz")))
    colnames(counts) <- readLines(file.path(mdir, "barcodes.tsv.gz"))

    pos <- read_csv(file.path(spatial_dir, "spatial", paste0(sid, "_spatial"), "tissue_positions_list.csv"),
                    col_names = c("barcode", "in_tissue", "array_row", "array_col", "pxl_row", "pxl_col"), show_col_types = FALSE)
    ann <- read_csv(file.path(spatial_dir, "metadata", paste0(sid, "_metadata.csv")), show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "unique_quiet") %>%
      transmute(barcode = `...1`, subtype, classification = Classification)
    spots <- tibble(barcode = colnames(counts), n_umi = colSums(counts), n_genes = colSums(counts > 0)) %>%
      left_join(pos, by = "barcode") %>%
      left_join(ann, by = "barcode") %>%
      mutate(qc_pass = in_tissue == 1 & !classification %in% "Artefact" & n_umi >= 500 & n_genes >= 250)

    keep <- spots$qc_pass
    list(counts = counts[, keep], spots = spots[keep, ], spots_all = spots,
         scalef = jsonlite::fromJSON(file.path(spatial_dir, "spatial", paste0(sid, "_spatial"), "scalefactors_json.json")))
  })
  qs_save(visium, sections_path)
}

spatial_qc <- bind_rows(lapply(names(visium), function(sid) {
  s <- visium[[sid]]$spots_all
  tibble(
    section = sid,
    subtype = unique(na.omit(s$subtype))[1],
    in_scrna_cohort = sid %in% wu_sc_samples | paste0(sid, "A") %in% wu_sc_samples,
    scrna_sample = c(intersect(c(sid, paste0(sid, "A")), wu_sc_samples), NA)[1],
    spots_in_tissue = sum(s$in_tissue == 1),
    spots_artefact = sum(s$classification %in% "Artefact"),
    spots_low_quality = sum(s$in_tissue == 1 & !s$classification %in% "Artefact" & (s$n_umi < 500 | s$n_genes < 250)),
    spots_qc = sum(s$qc_pass),
    median_umi = median(s$n_umi[s$qc_pass]),
    median_genes = median(s$n_genes[s$qc_pass]),
    genes_measured = nrow(visium[[sid]]$counts)
  )
}))
write_csv(spatial_qc, file.path(spatial_res_dir, "table_spatial_qc.csv"))
knitr::kable(spatial_qc, caption = "Wu et al. Visium sections: subtype, overlap with the scRNA-seq cohort and spot QC")

spatial_axis_genes <- c("FN1", "ITGA5", "ITGB1", "CCL5", "ACKR1", "CXCL12", "CXCR4", "MDK", "LRP1", "APP", "CD74")
axis_detection <- bind_rows(lapply(names(visium), function(sid) {
  cnt <- visium[[sid]]$counts
  tibble(section = sid, gene = spatial_axis_genes,
         measured = spatial_axis_genes %in% rownames(cnt),
         pct_spots_detected = sapply(spatial_axis_genes, function(g) if (g %in% rownames(cnt)) round(100 * mean(cnt[g, ] > 0), 1) else NA_real_))
}))
write_csv(axis_detection, file.path(spatial_res_dir, "table_spatial_axis_gene_detection.csv"))
knitr::kable(axis_detection %>% select(section, gene, pct_spots_detected) %>% tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = section, values_from = pct_spots_detected),
             caption = "Axis genes: percentage of QC spots with at least one UMI")
```

### Deconvolution with RCTD

Each spot holds several cells, so we estimate the cell-type composition of every spot with RCTD (`spacexr`, full mode) against the Wu single-cell data. The reference holds all 77,680 cells that pass QC, labeled with the harmonized taxonomy, except that endothelial cells are split into an ACKR1-positive venular class and the rest, giving nine classes with at most 3,000 randomly sampled cells each (seed 42). Weights are normalized to sum to 1 per spot, and for the FN1 and APP axes the endothelial weight is the sum of the two classes. As a sensitivity analysis, for the four sections whose patient is in the single-cell cohort, RCTD is rerun with a reference that leaves out that patient's cells. A finer reference, for the exploratory analyses, splits fibroblasts into myCAF-like and iCAF-like cells and T cells into CD8+, CD4+ and other. The RCTD weights are saved to `objects/revision/spatial/rctd_weights.qs2`.

```{r}
#| label: rev-spatial-rctd-run
#| eval: false
suppressMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
  library(qs2)
  library(Matrix)
  library(SeuratObject)
  library(spacexr)
})

set.seed(42)
num_cores <- parallel::detectCores() - 1
out_dir <- "objects/revision/spatial"
visium <- qs_read(file.path(out_dir, "visium_sections.qs2"))

seu_ref <- qs_read("objects/seu_wu_filtered.qs2")
ref_counts <- LayerData(seu_ref, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
ref_sample <- seu_ref$sample_id
rm(seu_ref)

wu_dirs <- list.dirs("data/raw/BCS014", full.names = FALSE, recursive = FALSE)
wu_meta <- bind_rows(lapply(wu_dirs, function(d) {
  read_csv(file.path("data/raw/BCS014", d, "metadata.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "unique_quiet") %>%
    transmute(barcode = paste0(d, "_", `...1`), celltype_major, celltype_minor)
}))
ref_meta <- wu_meta[match(colnames(ref_counts), wu_meta$barcode), ]

# Eight harmonized classes as in harmonize-wu-labels, with Endothelial split on the ACKR1+ venular subset
label_primary <- case_when(
  ref_meta$celltype_minor == "Endothelial ACKR1" ~ "Endothelial_ACKR1",
  ref_meta$celltype_major == "Endothelial" ~ "Endothelial_other",
  ref_meta$celltype_major == "CAFs" ~ "Fibroblast",
  ref_meta$celltype_major == "PVL" ~ "PVL",
  ref_meta$celltype_major %in% c("B-cells", "Plasmablasts") ~ "B_cell",
  ref_meta$celltype_major == "T-cells" ~ "T_cell",
  ref_meta$celltype_major == "Myeloid" ~ "Myeloid",
  ref_meta$celltype_major == "Normal Epithelial" ~ "Normal_epithelial",
  TRUE ~ "Cancer"
)
# Finer reference for exploratory analysis E3
label_fine <- case_when(
  ref_meta$celltype_minor == "CAFs myCAF-like" ~ "CAF_myCAF",
  ref_meta$celltype_major == "CAFs" ~ "CAF_iCAF",
  ref_meta$celltype_minor == "T cells CD8+" ~ "T_CD8",
  ref_meta$celltype_minor == "T cells CD4+" ~ "T_CD4",
  ref_meta$celltype_major == "T-cells" ~ "T_other",
  TRUE ~ label_primary
)
qs_save(data.frame(barcode = colnames(ref_counts), sample_id = ref_sample, label_primary, label_fine),
        file.path(out_dir, "rctd_reference_labels.qs2"))

build_reference <- function(labels, exclude_sample = NULL) {
  keep <- if (is.null(exclude_sample)) rep(TRUE, length(labels)) else ref_sample != exclude_sample
  set.seed(42)
  cells <- unlist(lapply(split(which(keep), labels[keep]), function(ix) if (length(ix) > 3000) sample(ix, 3000) else ix))
  counts <- ref_counts[, cells]
  Reference(counts, factor(setNames(labels[cells], colnames(counts))), nUMI = colSums(counts), n_max_cells = 3000)
}

run_rctd <- function(section, reference) {
  counts <- section$counts
  coords <- data.frame(x = section$spots$pxl_col, y = -section$spots$pxl_row, row.names = section$spots$barcode)
  puck <- SpatialRNA(coords, counts, nUMI = colSums(counts))
  rctd <- create.RCTD(puck, reference, max_cores = num_cores)
  rctd <- run.RCTD(rctd, doublet_mode = "full")
  as.matrix(normalize_weights(rctd@results$weights))
}

ref_primary <- build_reference(label_primary)
ref_fine <- build_reference(label_fine)

# Sections whose patient is also in the scRNA-seq cohort (Visium CID4290 is scRNA sample CID4290A)
overlap_sample <- c(CID4290 = "CID4290A", CID4465 = "CID4465", CID44971 = "CID44971", CID4535 = "CID4535")

weights_path <- file.path(out_dir, "rctd_weights.qs2")
rctd_weights <- if (file.exists(weights_path)) qs_read(weights_path) else list(primary = list(), fine = list(), lopo = list())
for (sid in names(visium)) {
  if (is.null(rctd_weights$primary[[sid]])) {
    message(sprintf("RCTD primary: %s", sid))
    rctd_weights$primary[[sid]] <- run_rctd(visium[[sid]], ref_primary)
    qs_save(rctd_weights, weights_path)
  }
}
for (sid in names(visium)) {
  if (is.null(rctd_weights$fine[[sid]])) {
    message(sprintf("RCTD fine: %s", sid))
    rctd_weights$fine[[sid]] <- run_rctd(visium[[sid]], ref_fine)
    qs_save(rctd_weights, weights_path)
  }
}
for (sid in names(overlap_sample)) {
  if (is.null(rctd_weights$lopo[[sid]])) {
    message(sprintf("RCTD leave-patient-out: %s", sid))
    rctd_weights$lopo[[sid]] <- run_rctd(visium[[sid]], build_reference(label_primary, exclude_sample = overlap_sample[[sid]]))
    qs_save(rctd_weights, weights_path)
  }
}
message("RCTD done")
```

Before testing anything we inspect the deconvolution. The median dominant-type weight per section and the mean weight of each class by pathologist annotation are reported below (@fig-spatial-weights-annotation). Dominant-type weights have medians of 0.43 to 0.80, and the cancer weight is highest in invasive-cancer spots, as expected. Absolute weights are skewed toward cancer even in stroma, so all tests use within-section ranks or rank correlations.

```{r}
#| label: rev-spatial-deconv-diagnostics
#| eval: true
rctd_weights <- qs_read(file.path(spatial_obj_dir, "rctd_weights.qs2"))

collapse_annotation <- function(x) {
  case_when(
    x %in% c("Stroma", "Stroma + adipose tissue") ~ "Stroma",
    x == "Invasive cancer" ~ "Invasive cancer",
    x == "Invasive cancer + stroma" ~ "Invasive cancer + stroma",
    x %in% c("Invasive cancer + lymphocytes", "Invasive cancer + adipose tissue + lymphocytes", "Cancer trapped in lymphocyte aggregation") ~ "Invasive cancer + lymphocytes",
    x == "Invasive cancer + stroma + lymphocytes" ~ "Invasive cancer + stroma + lymphocytes",
    x %in% c("Lymphocytes", "TLS") ~ "Lymphocytes / TLS",
    x %in% c("Normal glands + lymphocytes", "Normal + stroma + lymphocytes", "Normal duct", "DCIS") ~ "Normal / DCIS",
    TRUE ~ "Other"
  )
}
annotation_levels <- c("Invasive cancer", "Invasive cancer + stroma", "Invasive cancer + lymphocytes", "Invasive cancer + stroma + lymphocytes",
                       "Stroma", "Lymphocytes / TLS", "Normal / DCIS", "Other")
```

### Co-localization and co-expression tests

For each axis we run three tests in every section, and the section is the unit of replication, because spots within a section are not independent.

- **(a) Weight correlation.** Spearman's rho between the sender and receiver weights across spots, analyzed on the Fisher-z scale.
- **(b) Neighborhood enrichment.** A spot's neighborhood is the spot and its six immediate neighbors on the Visium hexagonal array. A spot is "high" for a cell type if its weight is at or above the 75th percentile of the section and at least 0.05. We count how often a sender-high spot has a receiver-high spot in its neighborhood and compare this with 1,000 permutations of the receiver-high labels across the section (seed 42). The effect is the log2 ratio of observed to expected counts. A label permutation ignores spatial autocorrelation, so we also compute the same enrichment for every pair of distinct cell types in the section and report the percentile of the axis pair among them, as a descriptive comparison.
- **(c) Ligand-receptor co-expression.** For each spot, the product of the mean ligand and the mean receptor expression over its neighborhood. The effect is Hedges' g between niche spots (neighborhoods holding both a sender-high and a receiver-high spot) and all other spots.

Section effects are pooled with a random-effects meta-analysis (REML) and Knapp-Hartung inference, which bases the test on the variation between sections. Within a family the p-values are corrected with Benjamini-Hochberg: the primary family is the three tests of FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1, the key secondary family the three tests of CCL5-ACKR1, and the exploratory family the tests of the other axes. A test meets our criterion when the pooled effect has the expected direction with q below 0.05 and the expected direction in at least five of the six sections. MDK-LRP1 is autocrine, so only test (c) applies.

```{r}
#| label: rev-spatial-helpers
#| eval: true
spatial_types <- c("Cancer", "Fibroblast", "Endothelial", "Endothelial_ACKR1", "Endothelial_other", "Myeloid", "T_cell", "B_cell", "PVL", "Normal_epithelial")
spatial_axes <- candidate_registry %>%
  transmute(axis_id, ligand, receptor, sender = sender_celltype,
            receiver = if_else(axis_id == "ccl5_ackr1", "Endothelial_ACKR1", receiver_celltype),
            family = case_when(axis_id == "fn1_itga5_itgb1" ~ "Primary", axis_id == "ccl5_ackr1" ~ "Key secondary", TRUE ~ "Exploratory axes"))

# Hexagonal distance in Visium doubled-column array coordinates, for all spot pairs up to max_d rings apart
hex_pairs <- function(spots, max_d = 3) {
  key <- paste(spots$array_row, spots$array_col)
  offs <- expand.grid(dr = -max_d:max_d, dc = (-2 * max_d):(2 * max_d)) %>%
    filter((dr + dc) %% 2 == 0) %>%
    mutate(d = abs(dr) + pmax(0, (abs(dc) - abs(dr)) / 2)) %>%
    filter(d <= max_d)
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(offs)), function(k) {
    data.frame(i = seq_len(nrow(spots)), j = match(paste(spots$array_row + offs$dr[k], spots$array_col + offs$dc[k]), key), d = offs$d[k])
  })) %>%
    filter(!is.na(j))
}

ring_adjacency <- function(sec, rings) {
  p <- sec$pairs[sec$pairs$d %in% rings, ]
  sparseMatrix(i = p$i, j = p$j, x = 1, dims = rep(nrow(sec$spots), 2))
}

prepare_section <- function(sid, w) {
  v <- visium[[sid]]
  spots <- v$spots[match(rownames(w), v$spots$barcode), ] %>% mutate(annotation = collapse_annotation(classification))
  w <- cbind(w, Endothelial = w[, "Endothelial_ACKR1"] + w[, "Endothelial_other"])
  counts <- v$counts[, spots$barcode]
  expr <- counts
  expr@x <- log1p(expr@x / rep(colSums(counts), diff(counts@p)) * 1e4)
  list(sid = sid, spots = spots, w = w, expr = expr, pairs = hex_pairs(spots))
}

subset_section <- function(sec, keep) {
  idx <- which(keep)
  new_index <- match(seq_len(nrow(sec$spots)), idx)
  list(sid = sec$sid, spots = sec$spots[idx, ], w = sec$w[idx, , drop = FALSE], expr = sec$expr[, idx],
       pairs = sec$pairs %>% mutate(i = new_index[i], j = new_index[j]) %>% filter(!is.na(i), !is.na(j)))
}

high_spots <- function(x, q = 0.75) as.numeric(x >= quantile(x, q) & x >= 0.05)
nb_mean <- function(A, x) as.vector(A %*% x) / rowSums(A)
gene_score <- function(expr, genes) {
  g <- strsplit(genes, "_")[[1]]
  if (!all(g %in% rownames(expr))) return(NULL)
  colMeans(as.matrix(expr[g, , drop = FALSE]))
}

spearman_stat <- function(x, y) {
  rho <- cor(x, y, method = "spearman")
  data.frame(est = atanh(rho), var = 1 / (length(x) - 3), rho = rho)
}

enrich_stat <- function(S, R, A, n_perm = 1000) {
  if (sum(S) < 10 || sum(R) < 10) return(data.frame(est = NA_real_, var = NA_real_, obs = NA_real_, expected = NA_real_, z = NA_real_, p_perm = NA_real_))
  obs <- sum(S * as.vector(A %*% R))
  set.seed(42)
  perm <- colSums(S * as.matrix(A %*% replicate(n_perm, sample(R))))
  e <- mean(perm)
  s <- sd(perm)
  data.frame(est = log2(obs / e), var = (s / (e * log(2)))^2, obs = obs, expected = e, z = (obs - e) / s, p_perm = (1 + sum(perm >= obs)) / (n_perm + 1))
}

hedges_g <- function(x, grp) {
  n1 <- sum(grp)
  n0 <- sum(!grp)
  sp <- sqrt(((n1 - 1) * var(x[grp]) + (n0 - 1) * var(x[!grp])) / (n1 + n0 - 2))
  if (n1 < 10 || n0 < 10 || !is.finite(sp) || sp == 0) return(data.frame(est = NA_real_, var = NA_real_))
  g <- (1 - 3 / (4 * (n1 + n0) - 9)) * (mean(x[grp]) - mean(x[!grp])) / sp
  data.frame(est = g, var = (n1 + n0) / (n1 * n0) + g^2 / (2 * (n1 + n0)))
}

# Random-effects (REML) pooling over sections with Knapp-Hartung inference
pool_sections <- function(est, v, expected_sign = 1) {
  keep <- is.finite(est) & is.finite(v)
  out <- data.frame(k = sum(keep), n_expected_dir = sum(sign(est[keep]) == expected_sign),
                    est = NA_real_, lo = NA_real_, hi = NA_real_, p = NA_real_, tau2 = NA_real_, i2 = NA_real_)
  if (sum(keep) < 2) return(out)
  fit <- rma(yi = est[keep], vi = v[keep], method = "REML", test = "knha", control = list(maxiter = 1000, stepadj = 0.5))
  out %>% mutate(est = fit$b[1], lo = fit$ci.lb, hi = fit$ci.ub, p = fit$pval, tau2 = fit$tau2, i2 = fit$I2)
}

# Niche of an axis: neighborhoods holding a sender-high and a receiver-high spot (any sender-high spot if autocrine)
axis_niche <- function(sec, ax, A, high_q = 0.75) {
  S <- high_spots(sec$w[, ax$sender], high_q)
  R <- high_spots(sec$w[, ax$receiver], high_q)
  niche <- if (ax$sender == ax$receiver) as.vector(A %*% S) > 0 else as.vector(A %*% S) > 0 & as.vector(A %*% R) > 0
  list(S = S, R = R, niche = niche, estimable = sum(S) >= 10 && sum(R) >= 10)
}

axis_section_tests <- function(sec, ax, rings = 0:1, high_q = 0.75, colocalisation = TRUE) {
  A <- ring_adjacency(sec, rings)
  nc <- axis_niche(sec, ax, A, high_q)
  lr <- nb_mean(A, gene_score(sec$expr, ax$ligand)) * nb_mean(A, gene_score(sec$expr, ax$receptor))
  rows <- list(hedges_g(lr, nc$niche) %>% mutate(test = "(c) L-R co-expression"))
  if (colocalisation && ax$sender != ax$receiver) {
    rows <- c(rows, list(
      spearman_stat(sec$w[, ax$sender], sec$w[, ax$receiver]) %>% mutate(test = "(a) weight correlation"),
      enrich_stat(nc$S, nc$R, A) %>% mutate(test = "(b) neighborhood enrichment")
    ))
  }
  out <- bind_rows(rows) %>% mutate(section = sec$sid, axis_id = ax$axis_id, n_spots = nrow(sec$spots),
                                    n_sender_high = sum(nc$S), n_receiver_high = sum(nc$R), n_niche = sum(nc$niche))
  out$est[out$test != "(a) weight correlation" & !nc$estimable] <- NA_real_
  out
}

run_axis_tests <- function(secs, axes = spatial_axes, ...) {
  bind_rows(lapply(secs, function(sec) bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(axes)), function(k) axis_section_tests(sec, axes[k, ], ...)))))
}

pool_axis_tests <- function(section_res, axes = spatial_axes) {
  section_res %>%
    group_by(axis_id, test) %>%
    group_modify(~ pool_sections(.x$est, .x$var)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    left_join(axes %>% select(axis_id, family), by = "axis_id") %>%
    group_by(family) %>%
    mutate(q_bh = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(criterion_met = !is.na(est) & est > 0 & q_bh < 0.05 & n_expected_dir >= 5)
}

fmt_pooled <- function(test, est, lo, hi) {
  ifelse(grepl("^\\(a\\)", test), sprintf("rho %.2f (%.2f to %.2f)", tanh(est), tanh(lo), tanh(hi)), sprintf("%.2f (%.2f to %.2f)", est, lo, hi))
}

secs_primary <- lapply(setNames(names(rctd_weights$primary), names(rctd_weights$primary)), function(sid) prepare_section(sid, rctd_weights$primary[[sid]]))
```

```{r}
#| label: rev-spatial-declared-tests
#| eval: true
spatial_section_res <- run_axis_tests(secs_primary)
spatial_pooled <- pool_axis_tests(spatial_section_res)
write_csv(spatial_section_res, file.path(spatial_res_dir, "spatial_tests_by_section.csv"))
write_csv(spatial_pooled, file.path(spatial_res_dir, "spatial_tests_pooled.csv"))

knitr::kable(
  spatial_pooled %>%
    mutate(family = factor(family, levels = c("Primary", "Key secondary", "Exploratory axes"))) %>%
    arrange(family, factor(axis_id, levels = spatial_axes$axis_id), test) %>%
    transmute(family, Axis = axis_labels[axis_id], test, k, `Pooled (95% CI)` = fmt_pooled(test, est, lo, hi),
              p = signif(p, 3), q = signif(q_bh, 3), `Expected direction` = paste0(n_expected_dir, "/", k), I2 = round(i2, 1), criterion_met),
  caption = "Tests: random-effects pooled estimates over sections (Knapp-Hartung), BH within each family. (a) Spearman rho; (b) log2 observed/expected co-occurrence; (c) Hedges' g of the L-R score, niche vs other spots"
)
knitr::kable(
  spatial_section_res %>%
    transmute(section, Axis = axis_labels[axis_id], test,
              estimate = ifelse(test == "(a) weight correlation", round(rho, 3), round(est, 3)), z = round(z, 1), p_perm = signif(p_perm, 2),
              n_spots, n_sender_high, n_receiver_high, n_niche) %>%
    arrange(Axis, test, section),
  caption = "Tests per section ((a) rho; (b) log2 O/E with permutation z and p; (c) Hedges' g)"
)

# Context-relative comparator for (b): rank of each axis pair among all pairs of distinct types
type_pairs <- as.data.frame(t(combn(spatial_types, 2)), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  setNames(c("type1", "type2")) %>%
  filter(!(type1 == "Endothelial" & grepl("^Endothelial_", type2)))
pair_enrichment <- bind_rows(lapply(secs_primary, function(sec) {
  A <- ring_adjacency(sec, 0:1)
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(type_pairs)), function(k) {
    enrich_stat(high_spots(sec$w[, type_pairs$type1[k]]), high_spots(sec$w[, type_pairs$type2[k]]), A) %>%
      mutate(section = sec$sid, type1 = type_pairs$type1[k], type2 = type_pairs$type2[k])
  }))
}))
write_csv(pair_enrichment, file.path(spatial_res_dir, "spatial_pair_enrichment_all_pairs.csv"))
hetero_axes <- spatial_axes %>% filter(sender != receiver)
axis_pair_rank <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(hetero_axes)), function(k) {
  ax <- hetero_axes[k, ]
  pair_enrichment %>%
    mutate(is_axis = (type1 == ax$sender & type2 == ax$receiver) | (type2 == ax$sender & type1 == ax$receiver)) %>%
    group_by(section) %>%
    summarise(axis_log2_oe = est[is_axis], percentile = 100 * mean(est[!is_axis] < est[is_axis], na.rm = TRUE),
              rank = if (is.finite(est[is_axis])) sum(est[!is_axis] > est[is_axis], na.rm = TRUE) + 1 else NA_real_,
              n_pairs = sum(is.finite(est)), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(axis_id = ax$axis_id)
}))
write_csv(axis_pair_rank, file.path(spatial_res_dir, "spatial_axis_pair_rank.csv"))
knitr::kable(
  axis_pair_rank %>% group_by(axis_id) %>%
    summarise(Axis = axis_labels[axis_id[1]], `Median percentile` = round(median(percentile, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
              `Percentile per section` = paste(round(percentile), collapse = ", "), `Rank per section` = paste(rank, collapse = ", "),
              Pairs = max(n_pairs)),
  caption = "(b) context-relative comparator: percentile of the axis pair's enrichment among all cell-type pairs in the same section (sections in the order 1142243F, 1160920F, CID4290, CID4465, CID44971, CID4535)"
)
```

The CCL5-ACKR1 axis meets the criterion for all three tests. T cells co-localize with ACKR1-positive venular endothelium in all six sections (log2 observed/expected `r sprintf("%.2f", spatial_pooled$est[spatial_pooled$axis_id == "ccl5_ackr1" & grepl("^\\(b\\)", spatial_pooled$test)])`, 95% CI `r sprintf("%.2f", spatial_pooled$lo[spatial_pooled$axis_id == "ccl5_ackr1" & grepl("^\\(b\\)", spatial_pooled$test)])` to `r sprintf("%.2f", spatial_pooled$hi[spatial_pooled$axis_id == "ccl5_ackr1" & grepl("^\\(b\\)", spatial_pooled$test)])`, q = `r sg(spatial_pooled$q_bh[spatial_pooled$axis_id == "ccl5_ackr1" & grepl("^\\(b\\)", spatial_pooled$test)], 2)`), and CCL5-ACKR1 co-expression is high in those niches (Hedges' g `r sprintf("%.2f", spatial_pooled$est[spatial_pooled$axis_id == "ccl5_ackr1" & grepl("^\\(c\\)", spatial_pooled$test)])`, q = `r sg(spatial_pooled$q_bh[spatial_pooled$axis_id == "ccl5_ackr1" & grepl("^\\(c\\)", spatial_pooled$test)], 2)`). Across cell-type pairs, the axis sits at the 89th percentile of enrichment (median over sections). For FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1, fibroblasts and endothelial cells co-localize in all six sections (log2 observed/expected `r sprintf("%.2f", spatial_pooled$est[spatial_pooled$axis_id == "fn1_itga5_itgb1" & grepl("^\\(b\\)", spatial_pooled$test)])`, q = `r sg(spatial_pooled$q_bh[spatial_pooled$axis_id == "fn1_itga5_itgb1" & grepl("^\\(b\\)", spatial_pooled$test)], 2)`), but the pair sits near the 57th percentile of all pairs. That is expected for stromal cells that share a compartment, and it is not an unusually strong contact. FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1 co-expression is higher in fibroblast-endothelial niches in five of six sections, and it misses our criterion (g `r sprintf("%.2f", spatial_pooled$est[spatial_pooled$axis_id == "fn1_itga5_itgb1" & grepl("^\\(c\\)", spatial_pooled$test)])`, q = `r sg(spatial_pooled$q_bh[spatial_pooled$axis_id == "fn1_itga5_itgb1" & grepl("^\\(c\\)", spatial_pooled$test)], 2)`).

### Benchmark against random gene pairs

A co-expression effect has to be judged against what any two genes of similar abundance would give. For each axis we draw 1,000 random gene pairs, with each gene matched to the corresponding axis gene within 2.5 percentiles of mean expression (genes detected in at least 1% of spots in every section, excluding the eleven axis genes), score them in the same niche, and pool them in the same way. The empirical p-value is one-sided. For FN1 we also draw random receptors matched to ITGA5 and ITGB1, and we compute the ligand-only and receptor-only scores, to see whether the co-expression is explained by FN1 alone.

```{r}
#| label: rev-spatial-benchmark
#| eval: true
bench_spatial_path <- file.path(spatial_obj_dir, "spatial_benchmark.qs2")

# Gene universe: measured in every section and detected in at least 1% of QC spots of each
shared_genes_sp <- Reduce(intersect, lapply(secs_primary, function(sec) rownames(sec$expr)))
universe <- shared_genes_sp[Reduce(`&`, lapply(secs_primary, function(sec) Matrix::rowMeans(sec$expr[shared_genes_sp, ] > 0) >= 0.01))]
gene_mean_all <- Reduce(`+`, lapply(secs_primary, function(sec) Matrix::rowSums(sec$expr[shared_genes_sp, ]))) /
  sum(sapply(secs_primary, function(sec) ncol(sec$expr)))
univ_ecdf <- ecdf(gene_mean_all[universe])
univ_pct <- univ_ecdf(gene_mean_all[universe])
pools <- lapply(setNames(spatial_axis_genes, spatial_axis_genes), function(g) {
  setdiff(universe[abs(univ_pct - univ_ecdf(gene_mean_all[g])) <= 0.025], spatial_axis_genes)
})

niches_primary <- lapply(secs_primary, function(sec) {
  A <- ring_adjacency(sec, 0:1)
  lapply(setNames(seq_len(nrow(spatial_axes)), spatial_axes$axis_id), function(k) axis_niche(sec, spatial_axes[k, ], A))
})

if (file.exists(bench_spatial_path)) {
  bench_sp <- qs_read(bench_spatial_path)
} else {
  set.seed(42)
  draws <- list()
  for (k in seq_len(nrow(spatial_axes))) {
    rec_genes <- strsplit(spatial_axes$receptor[k], "_")[[1]]
    lig_gene <- spatial_axes$ligand[k]
    draws[[spatial_axes$axis_id[k]]] <- lapply(seq_len(1000), function(j) {
      lig <- sample(pools[[lig_gene]], 1)
      list(lig = lig, rec = vapply(rec_genes, function(g) sample(setdiff(pools[[g]], lig), 1), character(1)))
    })
  }
  draws$fn1_random_receptor <- lapply(seq_len(1000), function(j) {
    list(lig = "FN1", rec = vapply(c("ITGA5", "ITGB1"), function(g) sample(pools[[g]], 1), character(1)))
  })

  needed <- unique(c(unlist(draws), spatial_axis_genes))
  nb_mats <- lapply(secs_primary, function(sec) {
    A <- ring_adjacency(sec, 0:1)
    sweep(as.matrix(sec$expr[needed, ] %*% t(A)), 2, rowSums(A), "/")
  })
  pooled_g <- function(axis_id, lig, rec) {
    gs <- bind_rows(lapply(names(secs_primary), function(sid) {
      nc <- niches_primary[[sid]][[axis_id]]
      if (!nc$estimable) return(data.frame(est = NA_real_, var = NA_real_))
      m <- nb_mats[[sid]]
      score <- if (length(lig) == 0) colMeans(m[rec, , drop = FALSE]) else if (length(rec) == 0) m[lig, ] else m[lig, ] * colMeans(m[rec, , drop = FALSE])
      hedges_g(score, nc$niche)
    }))
    pool_sections(gs$est, gs$var)$est
  }

  null_g <- bind_rows(lapply(names(draws), function(nm) {
    ax_id <- if (nm == "fn1_random_receptor") "fn1_itga5_itgb1" else nm
    g <- unlist(parallel::mclapply(draws[[nm]], function(dr) pooled_g(ax_id, dr$lig, dr$rec), mc.cores = num_cores))
    data.frame(null = nm, axis_id = ax_id, draw = seq_along(g), g = g,
               genes = vapply(draws[[nm]], function(dr) paste(dr$lig, paste(dr$rec, collapse = "_")), character(1)))
  }))
  single_gene <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(spatial_axes)), function(k) {
    rec_genes <- strsplit(spatial_axes$receptor[k], "_")[[1]]
    data.frame(axis_id = spatial_axes$axis_id[k],
               g_pair_check = pooled_g(spatial_axes$axis_id[k], spatial_axes$ligand[k], rec_genes),
               g_ligand_only = pooled_g(spatial_axes$axis_id[k], spatial_axes$ligand[k], character(0)),
               g_receptor_only = pooled_g(spatial_axes$axis_id[k], character(0), rec_genes))
  }))
  bench_sp <- list(null_g = null_g, single_gene = single_gene, n_universe = length(universe))
  qs_save(bench_sp, bench_spatial_path)
}

obs_c <- spatial_pooled %>% filter(test == "(c) L-R co-expression") %>% select(axis_id, g_obs = est)
bench_sp_summary <- bench_sp$null_g %>%
  left_join(obs_c, by = "axis_id") %>%
  group_by(null, axis_id) %>%
  summarise(g_obs = g_obs[1], n_null = sum(is.finite(g)), null_median = median(g, na.rm = TRUE), null_q95 = quantile(g, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
            percentile = 100 * mean(g < g_obs[1], na.rm = TRUE), emp_p_one_sided = (1 + sum(g >= g_obs[1], na.rm = TRUE)) / (n_null + 1), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(bench_sp$single_gene, by = "axis_id") %>%
  mutate(null = if_else(null == "fn1_random_receptor", "FN1 x random matched receptor", "Expression-matched random pairs"))
write_csv(bench_sp_summary, file.path(spatial_res_dir, "spatial_benchmark_random_pairs.csv"))
knitr::kable(
  bench_sp_summary %>% transmute(Axis = axis_labels[axis_id], null, `Observed g` = round(g_obs, 3), `Null median` = round(null_median, 3),
                                 `Null 95th pct` = round(null_q95, 3), Percentile = round(percentile, 1), `Empirical p (one-sided)` = signif(emp_p_one_sided, 3),
                                 `Ligand-only g` = round(g_ligand_only, 3), `Receptor-only g` = round(g_receptor_only, 3)),
  caption = sprintf("Benchmark of the (c) pooled Hedges' g against 1,000 expression-matched random gene pairs per axis (universe: %s genes), and the FN1-specific check", format(bench_sp$n_universe, big.mark = ","))
)

```

CCL5-ACKR1 co-expression exceeds all 1,000 random pairs, and FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1 co-expression exceeds 96% of them (@fig-spatial-benchmark). For FN1, however, the co-expression is explained by the ligand: a random receptor in place of ITGA5 and ITGB1 gives much the same effect. ACKR1 alone separates the CCL5 niches about as well as the pair does (g 1.70), so part of the CCL5-ACKR1 co-expression restates the co-localization, and the random-pair benchmark does not control for that.

```{r}
#| label: fig-spatial-benchmark
#| eval: true
#| fig-cap: "Pooled niche co-expression of each axis (vertical line) against 1,000 expression-matched random gene pairs; for FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1, also against FN1 paired with random receptors."
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.5
p_bench_sp <- ggplot(bench_sp$null_g %>% mutate(Axis = factor(axis_labels[axis_id], levels = axis_labels),
                                                null = if_else(null == "fn1_random_receptor", "FN1 x random receptor", "Random matched pairs")),
                     aes(x = g, fill = null)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5, color = NA) +
  geom_vline(data = obs_c %>% mutate(Axis = factor(axis_labels[axis_id], levels = axis_labels)), aes(xintercept = g_obs), linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~Axis, ncol = 5, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Random matched pairs" = "#56B4E9", "FN1 x random receptor" = "#E69F00")) +
  labs(x = "Pooled Hedges' g (niche vs other spots)", y = "Density", fill = NULL) +
  theme_publication() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
ggsave(file.path(spatial_res_dir, "fig_spatial_benchmark.png"), p_bench_sp, width = 12, height = 4.5, dpi = 300)
```

### Sensitivity analyses

Three variants test whether the main result depends on its settings: the leave-patient-out reference, "high" defined at the 90th instead of the 75th percentile, and a two-ring neighborhood (the spot plus 18 neighbors). The lead axes keep their direction in all of them, and the CCL5-ACKR1 result holds with the leave-patient-out reference, a stricter high cutoff and a wider neighborhood.

```{r}
#| label: rev-spatial-sensitivity
#| eval: true
secs_lopo <- secs_primary
for (sid in names(rctd_weights$lopo)) secs_lopo[[sid]] <- prepare_section(sid, rctd_weights$lopo[[sid]])

sens_section <- bind_rows(
  run_axis_tests(secs_lopo) %>% mutate(analysis = "S1 leave-patient-out reference"),
  run_axis_tests(secs_primary, high_q = 0.9) %>% mutate(analysis = "S2 high at 90th percentile"),
  run_axis_tests(secs_primary, rings = 0:2) %>% mutate(analysis = "S3 two-ring neighborhood")
)
sens_pooled <- sens_section %>%
  group_by(analysis) %>%
  group_modify(~ pool_axis_tests(.x)) %>%
  ungroup()
write_csv(sens_section, file.path(spatial_res_dir, "spatial_sensitivity_by_section.csv"))
write_csv(sens_pooled, file.path(spatial_res_dir, "spatial_sensitivity_pooled.csv"))
knitr::kable(
  bind_rows(spatial_pooled %>% mutate(analysis = "Main analysis"), sens_pooled) %>%
    filter(axis_id %in% c("fn1_itga5_itgb1", "ccl5_ackr1")) %>%
    arrange(factor(axis_id, levels = spatial_axes$axis_id), test, analysis) %>%
    transmute(Axis = axis_labels[axis_id], test, analysis, k, `Pooled (95% CI)` = fmt_pooled(test, est, lo, hi),
              q = signif(q_bh, 3), `Expected direction` = paste0(n_expected_dir, "/", k), criterion_met),
  caption = "Sensitivity analyses for the lead axes (BH within each family); all axes are in the CSV"
)
```

For HER2ST, a section enters the CCL5-ACKR1 tests only if ACKR1 is detected in at least 1% of its spots. Applying the same rule to the Visium sections removes 1142243F, where ACKR1 is detected in 0.2% of spots, and leaves the CCL5-ACKR1 result unchanged.

```{r}
#| label: rev-spatial-ackr1-detection
#| eval: true
low_ackr1 <- axis_detection %>% filter(gene == "ACKR1", pct_spots_detected < 1) %>% pull(section)
ackr1_filter_pooled <- pool_axis_tests(spatial_section_res %>% filter(axis_id == "ccl5_ackr1", !section %in% low_ackr1)) %>%
  mutate(sections_excluded = paste(low_ackr1, collapse = ", "))
write_csv(ackr1_filter_pooled, file.path(spatial_res_dir, "spatial_ccl5_ackr1_detection_filter.csv"))
knitr::kable(
  ackr1_filter_pooled %>%
    transmute(test, k, `Pooled (95% CI)` = fmt_pooled(test, est, lo, hi), q = signif(q_bh, 3),
              `Expected direction` = paste0(n_expected_dir, "/", k), criterion_met),
  caption = "CCL5-ACKR1 without the sections in which ACKR1 is detected in fewer than 1% of spots"
)
```

### Exploratory analyses

Further analyses probe the lead axes and are corrected as one family. They cover spots annotated as stroma (E1), the tumor-stroma boundary (E2), finer cell-type subsets from the second RCTD reference (E3, myCAF-like and iCAF-like senders and CD8+ T-cell senders), the enrichment as a function of distance (E4), the co-expression of every measurable consensus interaction in its own niche (E5), the FN1 receiver program and the endothelial MHC-II program within endothelial-high spots (E6), and T-cell weight around FN1-high stroma (E7).

```{r}
#| label: rev-spatial-exploratory
#| eval: true
secs_fine <- lapply(setNames(names(rctd_weights$fine), names(rctd_weights$fine)), function(sid) prepare_section(sid, rctd_weights$fine[[sid]]))
lead_axes <- spatial_axes %>% filter(axis_id %in% c("fn1_itga5_itgb1", "ccl5_ackr1"))
fn1_axis <- spatial_axes %>% filter(axis_id == "fn1_itga5_itgb1")

# E1: stroma-annotated spots only
e1 <- bind_rows(lapply(secs_primary, function(sec) {
  keep <- sec$spots$annotation == "Stroma"
  if (sum(keep) < 30) return(NULL)
  run_axis_tests(list(subset_section(sec, keep)), axes = lead_axes)
})) %>% mutate(analysis = "E1 stroma spots", label = paste(axis_labels[axis_id], test))

# E2: FN1 L-R score at the tumor-stroma boundary
e2 <- bind_rows(lapply(secs_primary, function(sec) {
  A <- ring_adjacency(sec, 0:1)
  boundary <- as.vector(A %*% high_spots(sec$w[, "Cancer"])) > 0 & as.vector(A %*% high_spots(sec$w[, "Fibroblast"])) > 0
  lr <- nb_mean(A, gene_score(sec$expr, "FN1")) * nb_mean(A, gene_score(sec$expr, "ITGA5_ITGB1"))
  hedges_g(lr, boundary) %>% mutate(section = sec$sid, n_niche = sum(boundary))
})) %>% mutate(analysis = "E2 tumor-stroma boundary", axis_id = "fn1_itga5_itgb1", test = "(c) L-R co-expression", label = "FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1 L-R score, boundary vs other spots")

# E3: CAF and T-cell subsets from the finer reference
subset_axes <- tibble::tribble(
  ~axis_id, ~ligand, ~receptor, ~sender, ~receiver, ~label,
  "fn1_itga5_itgb1", "FN1", "ITGA5_ITGB1", "CAF_myCAF", "Endothelial", "FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1, myCAF-like sender",
  "fn1_itga5_itgb1", "FN1", "ITGA5_ITGB1", "CAF_iCAF", "Endothelial", "FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1, iCAF-like sender",
  "ccl5_ackr1", "CCL5", "ACKR1", "T_CD8", "Endothelial_ACKR1", "CCL5-ACKR1, CD8+ T-cell sender"
)
e3 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(subset_axes)), function(k) {
  run_axis_tests(secs_fine, axes = subset_axes[k, ]) %>% filter(test != "(a) weight correlation") %>% mutate(label = paste(subset_axes$label[k], test))
})) %>% mutate(analysis = "E3 subsets")

# E6: FN1 receiver program and endothelial MHC-II within endothelial-high spots
e6_genes_path <- file.path(spatial_obj_dir, "e6_programme_genes.qs2")
if (file.exists(e6_genes_path)) {
  e6_genes <- qs_read(e6_genes_path)
} else {
  fn1_up <- read_csv("results/revision/pseudobulk_pooled_de_all.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    filter(axis_id == "fn1_itga5_itgb1", FDR < 0.05, logFC > 0) %>%
    pull(gene)
  ref_labels <- qs_read(file.path(spatial_obj_dir, "rctd_reference_labels.qs2"))
  ref_counts <- SeuratObject::LayerData(qs_read("objects/seu_wu_filtered.qs2"), assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
  lib_size <- Matrix::colSums(ref_counts)
  ref_lognorm <- log1p(t(t(as.matrix(ref_counts[intersect(fn1_up, rownames(ref_counts)), ])) / lib_size * 1e4))
  fib_mean <- rowMeans(ref_lognorm[, ref_labels$label_primary == "Fibroblast"])
  endo_mean <- rowMeans(ref_lognorm[, grepl("^Endothelial", ref_labels$label_primary)])
  e6_genes <- list(fn1_up = fn1_up, fn1_programme = names(which(endo_mean >= fib_mean)),
                   mhc2 = c("HLA-DRA", "HLA-DRB1", "HLA-DPA1", "HLA-DPB1", "HLA-DMA", "CD74", "CIITA"))
  qs_save(e6_genes, e6_genes_path)
}
programme_score <- function(sec, genes) {
  g <- intersect(genes, rownames(sec$expr))
  colMeans(t(scale(t(as.matrix(sec$expr[g, , drop = FALSE])))), na.rm = TRUE)
}
e6 <- bind_rows(lapply(secs_primary, function(sec) {
  A <- ring_adjacency(sec, 0:1)
  endo_high <- high_spots(sec$w[, "Endothelial"]) == 1
  lr <- nb_mean(A, gene_score(sec$expr, "FN1")) * nb_mean(A, gene_score(sec$expr, "ITGA5_ITGB1"))
  bind_rows(
    spearman_stat(lr[endo_high], programme_score(sec, e6_genes$fn1_programme)[endo_high]) %>% mutate(label = "FN1 L-R score vs FN1 receiver program (endothelial-high spots)", expected_sign = 1),
    spearman_stat(lr[endo_high], programme_score(sec, e6_genes$mhc2)[endo_high]) %>% mutate(label = "FN1 L-R score vs MHC-II score (endothelial-high spots)", expected_sign = -1)
  ) %>% mutate(section = sec$sid, n_niche = sum(endo_high))
})) %>% mutate(analysis = "E6 receiver program", axis_id = "fn1_itga5_itgb1", test = "rho")

# E7: T-cell weight in FN1-high neighborhoods
e7 <- bind_rows(lapply(names(secs_primary), function(sid) {
  sec <- secs_primary[[sid]]
  A <- ring_adjacency(sec, 0:1)
  fn1_nb <- nb_mean(A, gene_score(sec$expr, "FN1"))
  fn1_high <- fn1_nb >= quantile(fn1_nb, 0.75)
  cd8 <- secs_fine[[sid]]$w[rownames(sec$w), "T_CD8"]
  bind_rows(
    hedges_g(sec$w[, "T_cell"], fn1_high) %>% mutate(label = "T-cell weight, FN1-high neighborhoods vs other spots"),
    hedges_g(cd8, fn1_high) %>% mutate(label = "CD8+ T-cell weight, FN1-high neighborhoods vs other spots")
  ) %>% mutate(section = sid, n_niche = sum(fn1_high), expected_sign = -1)
})) %>% mutate(analysis = "E7 immune exclusion", axis_id = "fn1_itga5_itgb1", test = "g")

exploratory_section <- bind_rows(e1, e2, e3, e6, e7) %>% mutate(expected_sign = coalesce(expected_sign, 1))
exploratory_pooled <- exploratory_section %>%
  group_by(analysis, label) %>%
  group_modify(~ pool_sections(.x$est, .x$var, expected_sign = .x$expected_sign[1]) %>% mutate(expected_sign = .x$expected_sign[1], test = .x$test[1])) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(q_bh = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"),
         criterion_met = !is.na(est) & sign(est) == expected_sign & q_bh < 0.05 & n_expected_dir >= 5)
write_csv(exploratory_section, file.path(spatial_res_dir, "spatial_exploratory_by_section.csv"))
write_csv(exploratory_pooled, file.path(spatial_res_dir, "spatial_exploratory_pooled.csv"))
knitr::kable(
  exploratory_pooled %>%
    transmute(analysis, label, k, `Expected sign` = expected_sign,
              `Pooled (95% CI)` = ifelse(test %in% c("(a) weight correlation", "rho"), sprintf("rho %.2f (%.2f to %.2f)", tanh(est), tanh(lo), tanh(hi)), sprintf("%.2f (%.2f to %.2f)", est, lo, hi)),
              p = signif(p, 3), q = signif(q_bh, 3), `Expected direction` = paste0(n_expected_dir, "/", k), criterion_met),
  caption = "Exploratory family (BH across all rows): pooled over sections, random effects with Knapp-Hartung"
)
```


```{r}
#| label: spatial-consensus-coexpression
#| eval: true
# E5: niche co-expression of every measurable consensus interaction in its own sender-receiver niche (descriptive)
consensus_sp <- read_csv("results/cross_cohort_comparison/consensus_interactions_all.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  distinct(Source, Target, Ligand, Receptor) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  filter(all(c(strsplit(Ligand, "_")[[1]], strsplit(Receptor, "_")[[1]]) %in% shared_genes_sp)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  transmute(axis_id = paste(Source, Target, Ligand, Receptor, sep = "|"), ligand = Ligand, receptor = Receptor, sender = Source, receiver = Target)
e5_section <- run_axis_tests(secs_primary, axes = consensus_sp, colocalisation = FALSE)
e5 <- e5_section %>%
  group_by(axis_id) %>%
  group_modify(~ pool_sections(.x$est, .x$var)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(percentile = 100 * (rank(est, na.last = "keep") - 1) / (sum(is.finite(est)) - 1)) %>%
  tidyr::separate(axis_id, c("sender", "receiver", "ligand", "receptor"), sep = "\\|", remove = FALSE) %>%
  arrange(desc(est))
write_csv(e5, file.path(spatial_res_dir, "spatial_consensus_pairs_coexpression.csv"))
knitr::kable(
  e5 %>%
    filter(paste(ligand, receptor) %in% paste(candidate_registry$ligand, candidate_registry$receptor)) %>%
    transmute(Interaction = paste0(ligand, "-", receptor, " (", sender, " to ", receiver, ")"), `Pooled g` = round(est, 3),
              `Expected direction` = paste0(n_expected_dir, "/", k), Percentile = round(percentile, 1), Rank = match(axis_id, e5$axis_id)),
  caption = sprintf("E5: the five axes among %d measurable consensus interactions, each scored in its own niche (Endothelial = both classes summed)", sum(is.finite(e5$est)))
)
```

The exploratory results support the lead axes in some places and not in others. The CCL5-ACKR1 niches are concentrated in lymphocyte-rich regions and tertiary lymphoid structures (4.2-fold enrichment in lymphocyte and TLS spots), and with CD8+ T cells as the sender the co-expression remains clearly positive (g 1.26, q = 0.027). Within endothelial-high spots, FN1 co-expression tracks the endothelial basement-membrane and angiogenic program from the pseudobulk analysis (rho 0.35, q = 0.006). For FN1, co-expression with myCAF-like senders is positive in all six sections (g 0.72) but not significant (q = 0.066), and the iCAF-like result is null. Two things did not hold. We did not see immune exclusion around FN1-high stroma: T-cell weight is higher, not lower, there in four of six sections, so immune exclusion rests on the bulk CD8+ association alone. And we did not find the reduced endothelial MHC-II program in the spatial data, so we present it as a pseudobulk observation only. Among the other axes, CXCL12-CXCR4 co-expression is positive in all six sections (g 0.99, q = 0.007) and MDK-LRP1 is as well (g 0.70, q = 0.025, autocrine), whereas APP-CD74 co-localizes weakly (rho 0.26, q = 0.007) with null co-expression (g 0.03). These three are exploratory.

### Histological context

The distribution of niche spots across the pathologist's annotation categories shows where each niche sits (descriptive, no test).

```{r}
#| label: rev-spatial-histology

niche_annotation <- bind_rows(lapply(secs_primary, function(sec) {

           classification = sec$spots$classification, niche = niches_primary[[sec$sid]][[spatial_axes$axis_id[k]]]$niche)
  }))
}))
histology_table <- niche_annotation %>%
  group_by(axis_id, annotation) %>%
  summarise(niche_spots = sum(niche), all_spots = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%

  mutate(pct_of_niche = 100 * niche_spots / sum(niche_spots), pct_of_all = 100 * all_spots / sum(all_spots),
         pct_niche_within_category = 100 * niche_spots / all_spots) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(annotation = factor(annotation, levels = annotation_levels)) %>%

histology_by_section <- niche_annotation %>%
```

### Maps

For each axis, the maps show the H&E image beside the sender weight, the receiver weight and the ligand-receptor co-expression score of the neighborhoods, for the representative section (the section whose co-expression effect is closest to the pooled estimate; @fig-spatial-rep-fn1_itga5_itgb1 and @fig-spatial-rep-ccl5_ackr1) and for all six sections. Colors are scaled per panel.

```{r}
#| label: rev-spatial-figures
#| eval: true
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 20
library(png)

spot_map <- function(sec, values, title, palette = "magma") {
  ggplot(data.frame(x = sec$spots$pxl_col, y = -sec$spots$pxl_row, v = values), aes(x = x, y = y, color = v)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.55) +
    scale_color_viridis_c(option = palette, name = NULL) +
    coord_fixed(xlim = range(sec$spots$pxl_col) + c(-150, 150), ylim = -rev(range(sec$spots$pxl_row)) + c(-150, 150), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme_void(base_size = 13) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5), legend.key.height = unit(0.6, "cm"), legend.key.width = unit(0.35, "cm"))
}
# H&E drawn in full-resolution pixel coordinates, so it lines up with the spot maps
he_panel <- function(sid, title) {
  img <- readPNG(file.path(spatial_dir, "spatial", paste0(sid, "_spatial"), "tissue_lowres_image.png"))
  sc <- visium[[sid]]$scalef$tissue_lowres_scalef
  sp <- visium[[sid]]$spots
  pad <- 150
  ggplot() +
    annotation_raster(img, xmin = 0, xmax = dim(img)[2] / sc, ymin = -dim(img)[1] / sc, ymax = 0) +
    coord_fixed(xlim = range(sp$pxl_col) + c(-pad, pad), ylim = -rev(range(sp$pxl_row)) + c(-pad, pad), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme_void(base_size = 13) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))
}
axis_row <- function(ax, sid) {
  sec <- secs_primary[[sid]]
  A <- ring_adjacency(sec, 0:1)
  lr <- nb_mean(A, gene_score(sec$expr, ax$ligand)) * nb_mean(A, gene_score(sec$expr, ax$receptor))
  he_panel(sid, sprintf("H&E (%s)", sid)) +
    spot_map(sec, sec$w[, ax$sender], paste("Sender:", ax$sender), "viridis") +
    spot_map(sec, sec$w[, ax$receiver], paste("Receiver:", ax$receiver), "viridis") +
    spot_map(sec, lr, sprintf("%s x %s (neighborhood)", ax$ligand, gsub("_", "/", ax$receptor)), "magma") +
    plot_layout(nrow = 1)
}

representative <- spatial_section_res %>%
  filter(test == "(c) L-R co-expression", is.finite(est)) %>%
  left_join(spatial_pooled %>% filter(test == "(c) L-R co-expression") %>% select(axis_id, pooled = est), by = "axis_id") %>%
  group_by(axis_id) %>%
  slice_min(abs(est - pooled), n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(axis_id, section, g = est, pooled)
write_csv(representative, file.path(spatial_res_dir, "spatial_representative_sections.csv"))

fig1 <- wrap_plots(lapply(spatial_axes$axis_id, function(a) axis_row(spatial_axes[spatial_axes$axis_id == a, ], representative$section[representative$axis_id == a])), ncol = 1)
ggsave(file.path(spatial_res_dir, "fig1_spatial_representative.png"), fig1, width = 14, height = 19, dpi = 300)

for (a in spatial_axes$axis_id) {
  figs <- wrap_plots(lapply(names(secs_primary), function(sid) axis_row(spatial_axes[spatial_axes$axis_id == a, ], sid)), ncol = 1)
  ggsave(file.path(spatial_res_dir, sprintf("figS_spatial_%s_all_sections.png", a)), figs, width = 14, height = 23, dpi = 200)
}
```

## HER2ST: an independent spatial cohort

The Wu sections overlap with the discovery cohort, so we sought an independent spatial dataset. HER2ST (Andersson et al. 2021, Zenodo 4751624) comes from eight HER2-positive patients who are not in the discovery cohorts, so unlike the Wu sections it is an independent patient population. The Wu single-cell data are used only as the reference for deconvolution. The data are 36 sections with 100 µm spots, from eight patients (A to H). Patients A to D have six serial sections each and patients E to H have three. Because serial sections of one tumor are not independent, the unit of replication is the patient, and our primary analysis uses one pathologist-labeled section per patient (A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G2 and H1; k = 8). As a sensitivity analysis we use all 36 sections and average the effects within patient before pooling.

We apply the same deconvolution (RCTD in full mode with the Wu reference of nine classes), the same three tests and the same definitions as for Visium, with two changes forced by the platform. The legacy symbol DARC is mapped to ACKR1, and a section is not estimable for CCL5-ACKR1 if ACKR1 is detected in fewer than 1% of its spots. The 100 µm lattice has no fixed six-neighbor layout, so the neighborhood of a spot is the spot plus all spots within 1.5 times the median nearest-neighbor distance of the section. We test only the two lead axes, and we correct the six tests (FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1 and CCL5-ACKR1, tests a to c) as one Benjamini-Hochberg family. A test replicates if the pooled HER2ST effect has the same sign as the Wu pooled estimate, q is below 0.05, and the sign agrees in at least six of the eight patients. A hypothesis replicates if its co-localization test (b) replicates, and its co-expression test (c) is reported alongside. A second sensitivity analysis uses a two-ring neighborhood (2.5 times the median distance).

RCTD is run on the 36 sections.

```{r}
#| label: rev-her2st-rctd-run
#| eval: false
suppressMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(readr)
  library(qs2)
  library(SeuratObject)
  library(spacexr)
  library(data.table)
})

set.seed(42)
her2_obj_dir <- "objects/revision/her2st"
dir.create(her2_obj_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
her2_sections <- c(sprintf("%s%d", rep(LETTERS[1:4], each = 6), rep(1:6, 4)), sprintf("%s%d", rep(LETTERS[5:8], each = 3), rep(1:3, 4)))

seu_ref <- qs_read("objects/seu_wu_filtered.qs2")
ref_counts <- LayerData(seu_ref, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
rm(seu_ref)

# Reference labels are those of the Visium RCTD run, so the reference is identical
ref_labels <- qs_read("objects/revision/spatial/rctd_reference_labels.qs2")
label_primary <- setNames(ref_labels$label_primary, ref_labels$barcode)[colnames(ref_counts)]

build_reference <- function(labels) {
  cells <- unlist(lapply(split(seq_along(labels), labels), function(ix) if (length(ix) > 3000) sample(ix, 3000) else ix))
  counts <- ref_counts[, cells]
  Reference(counts, factor(setNames(labels[cells], colnames(counts))), nUMI = colSums(counts), n_max_cells = 3000)
}
ref_primary <- build_reference(label_primary)

for (sid in her2_sections) {
  out_path <- file.path(her2_obj_dir, paste0("her2st_", sid, ".qs2"))
  if (file.exists(out_path)) next

  expr <- fread(file.path("data/spatial/her2st/counts/count-matrices", paste0(sid, ".tsv.gz")))
  spot_names <- expr[[1]]
  counts_all <- t(as.matrix(expr[, -1, with = FALSE]))
  colnames(counts_all) <- spot_names
  rm(expr)

  sel <- fread(file.path("data/spatial/her2st/spots", paste0(sid, "_selection.tsv.gz")))
  sel <- sel[selected == 1]
  sel$name <- paste0(sel$x, "x", sel$y)
  keep <- intersect(sel$name, colnames(counts_all))
  counts <- counts_all[, keep, drop = FALSE]
  counts <- counts[rowSums(counts) > 0, , drop = FALSE]
  spots <- sel[match(keep, sel$name), ]

  coords <- data.frame(x = spots$pixel_x, y = -spots$pixel_y, row.names = keep)
  puck <- SpatialRNA(coords, counts, nUMI = colSums(counts))
  rctd <- create.RCTD(puck, ref_primary, max_cores = 1)
  rctd <- run.RCTD(rctd, doublet_mode = "full")
  weights <- as.matrix(normalize_weights(rctd@results$weights))

  qs_save(list(weights = weights, spots = spots, counts = counts), out_path)
}
```

We then define the neighborhoods and report the quality of the sections, including the ACKR1 detection that decides whether the CCL5 tests are estimable.

```{r}
#| label: rev-her2st-data
#| eval: true
her2_obj_dir <- "objects/revision/her2st"
her2_res_dir <- "results/revision/her2st"
dir.create(her2_res_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
her2_sections <- c(sprintf("%s%d", rep(LETTERS[1:4], each = 6), rep(1:6, 4)), sprintf("%s%d", rep(LETTERS[5:8], each = 3), rep(1:3, 4)))
her2_primary <- c("A1", "B1", "C1", "D1", "E1", "F1", "G2", "H1")
her2_axes <- spatial_axes %>% filter(axis_id %in% c("fn1_itga5_itgb1", "ccl5_ackr1"))

# Neighborhood on the ST lattice: spots within 1.5 (d = 1) or 2.5 (d = 2) times the median nearest-neighbor distance
prepare_her2st <- function(sid) {
  obj <- qs_read(file.path(her2_obj_dir, paste0("her2st_", sid, ".qs2")))
  w <- obj$weights
  spots <- obj$spots[match(rownames(w), obj$spots$name), ]
  w <- cbind(w, Endothelial = w[, "Endothelial_ACKR1"] + w[, "Endothelial_other"])
  counts <- obj$counts[, rownames(w), drop = FALSE]
  rownames(counts)[rownames(counts) == "DARC"] <- "ACKR1"
  # A gene with no counts in the section is dropped at QC, so it is restored as zeros (0% detected)
  if (!"ACKR1" %in% rownames(counts)) counts <- rbind(counts, ACKR1 = 0)
  expr <- Matrix::Matrix(counts, sparse = TRUE)
  expr@x <- log1p(expr@x / rep(colSums(counts), diff(expr@p)) * 1e4)
  D <- as.matrix(dist(cbind(spots$pixel_x, spots$pixel_y)))
  m <- median(apply(D + diag(Inf, nrow(D)), 1, min))
  pr <- which(D <= 2.5 * m & row(D) != col(D), arr.ind = TRUE)
  pairs <- rbind(data.frame(i = pr[, 1], j = pr[, 2], d = ifelse(D[pr] <= 1.5 * m, 1, 2)),
                 data.frame(i = seq_len(nrow(D)), j = seq_len(nrow(D)), d = 0))
  list(sid = sid, patient = substr(sid, 1, 1), spots = spots, w = w, expr = expr, pairs = pairs,
       ackr1_pct = if ("ACKR1" %in% rownames(counts)) 100 * mean(counts["ACKR1", ] > 0) else 0)
}
her2_secs <- lapply(setNames(her2_sections, her2_sections), prepare_her2st)

her2_qc <- bind_rows(lapply(her2_secs, function(s) {
  tibble(section = s$sid, patient = s$patient, primary = s$sid %in% her2_primary, spots = nrow(s$spots),
         median_umi = median(colSums(s$expr > 0)), ackr1_pct_spots = round(s$ackr1_pct, 2),
         median_dominant_weight = median(apply(s$w, 1, max)))
}))
write_csv(her2_qc, file.path(her2_res_dir, "table_her2st_qc_diagnostics.csv"))
knitr::kable(her2_qc, digits = 2, caption = "HER2ST sections: spots, ACKR1 detection and RCTD dominant-type weight (primary sections marked)")
```

The pooled tests over the eight patients are next, in the same table as the pooled Wu estimates for direct comparison.

```{r}
#| label: rev-her2st-tests
#| eval: true
# Pooled over patients (k = 8). A patient-level estimate is the mean over its sections when S-all is used.
wu_pooled <- read_csv("results/revision/spatial/spatial_tests_pooled.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(axis_id %in% c("fn1_itga5_itgb1", "ccl5_ackr1")) %>%
  select(axis_id, test, wu_est = est)

her2_test_pool <- function(section_res) {
  section_res %>%
    group_by(axis_id, test) %>%
    group_modify(~ pool_sections(.x$est, .x$var)) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# ACKR1 must be detected in at least 1% of spots for the CCL5 tests
her2_run <- function(secs, rings = 0:1) {
  res <- NULL
  for (s in secs) res <- bind_rows(res, run_axis_tests(list(s), axes = her2_axes, rings = rings))
  ackr1_ok <- sapply(secs, function(s) s$ackr1_pct >= 1)
  res$est[res$axis_id == "ccl5_ackr1" & !ackr1_ok[res$section]] <- NA_real_
  res
}

her2_primary_res <- her2_run(her2_secs[her2_primary])
her2_primary_pool <- her2_test_pool(her2_primary_res)

# S-all: section estimates are averaged within patient, then pooled over the 8 patients
her2_all_res <- her2_run(her2_secs)
her2_all_patient <- her2_all_res %>%
  group_by(patient = substr(section, 1, 1), axis_id, test) %>%
  summarise(est = mean(est, na.rm = TRUE), var = mean(var, na.rm = TRUE) / n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(est = ifelse(is.nan(est), NA_real_, est))
her2_all_pool <- her2_all_patient %>% group_by(axis_id, test) %>% group_modify(~ pool_sections(.x$est, .x$var)) %>% ungroup()

# S-2ring: two-ring neighborhood
her2_2ring_res <- her2_run(her2_secs[her2_primary], rings = 0:2)
her2_2ring_pool <- her2_test_pool(her2_2ring_res)

declared <- her2_primary_pool %>%
  left_join(wu_pooled, by = c("axis_id", "test")) %>%
  mutate(n_same_dir = sapply(seq_len(n()), function(k) {
    e <- her2_primary_res$est[her2_primary_res$axis_id == axis_id[k] & her2_primary_res$test == test[k]]
    sum(e > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  }))
declared$q_bh6 <- p.adjust(declared$p, method = "BH")
declared$criterion_met <- !is.na(declared$est) & sign(declared$est) == sign(declared$wu_est) &
  declared$q_bh6 < 0.05 & declared$n_same_dir >= 6
write_csv(declared, file.path(her2_res_dir, "her2st_declared_tests_pooled.csv"))
write_csv(her2_primary_res, file.path(her2_res_dir, "her2st_declared_tests_by_section.csv"))

knitr::kable(
  declared %>%
    transmute(Axis = axis_labels[axis_id], test, k, `HER2ST pooled (95% CI)` = fmt_pooled(test, est, lo, hi),
              `Wu pooled` = round(wu_est, 3), p = signif(p, 3), q = signif(q_bh6, 3),
              `Same direction (of 8)` = n_same_dir, `Replicated` = criterion_met),
  caption = "HER2ST tests, primary (one labeled section per patient, k = 8). BH across the six tests; criterion as defined in the text"
)
knitr::kable(
  bind_rows(her2_all_pool %>% mutate(analysis = "S-all (36 sections, patient-averaged)"),
            her2_2ring_pool %>% mutate(analysis = "S-2ring (primary sections)")) %>%
    transmute(analysis, Axis = axis_labels[axis_id], test, k, `Pooled (95% CI)` = fmt_pooled(test, est, lo, hi), p = signif(p, 3)),
  caption = "HER2ST sensitivity analyses; reported in full, not used to change the primary result"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: her2st-summary-text
#| eval: true
her2_pick <- function(col, ax, tst) declared[[col]][declared$axis_id == ax & grepl(tst, declared$test, fixed = TRUE)]
```

HER2ST is directionally consistent with the CCL5-ACKR1 result without meeting the criterion. For co-expression (c), the pooled effect is `r sprintf("%.2f", her2_pick("est", "ccl5_ackr1", "(c)"))` (`r sprintf("%.2f", her2_pick("lo", "ccl5_ackr1", "(c)"))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", her2_pick("hi", "ccl5_ackr1", "(c)"))`), against `r sprintf("%.2f", her2_pick("wu_est", "ccl5_ackr1", "(c)"))` in Wu, with the same sign in `r her2_pick("n_same_dir", "ccl5_ackr1", "(c)")` of the `r her2_pick("k", "ccl5_ackr1", "(c)")` estimable patients, nominal p = `r sg(her2_pick("p", "ccl5_ackr1", "(c)"), 2)` and q = `r sg(her2_pick("q_bh6", "ccl5_ackr1", "(c)"), 2)` across the six tests. The weight correlation (a) is positive in `r her2_pick("n_same_dir", "ccl5_ackr1", "(a)")` of `r her2_pick("k", "ccl5_ackr1", "(a)")` patients, and the neighborhood enrichment (b) in `r her2_pick("n_same_dir", "ccl5_ackr1", "(b)")` of `r her2_pick("k", "ccl5_ackr1", "(b)")`. Section A1 is not estimable for CCL5-ACKR1, because ACKR1 is detected in only 0.6% of its spots. The CCL5-ACKR1 signal is therefore consistent in direction across independent patients, which is supportive, but it does not clear our correction, so we call it directionally consistent and not a replication. FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1 is not replicated: its three tests have pooled effects of `r sprintf("%.2f", her2_pick("est", "fn1_itga5_itgb1", "(a)"))` (rho), `r sprintf("%.2f", her2_pick("est", "fn1_itga5_itgb1", "(b)"))` and `r sprintf("%.2f", her2_pick("est", "fn1_itga5_itgb1", "(c)"))`, with q of at least `r sg(min(declared$q_bh6[declared$axis_id == "fn1_itga5_itgb1"]), 2)`. Averaging all 36 sections within patient gives a nominally significant CCL5-ACKR1 co-expression effect, but this sensitivity analysis is not corrected for multiplicity, so we report it only as such. With a family of three tests per hypothesis, as used for Visium, the CCL5-ACKR1 co-expression test would have q = 0.035. We do not use that figure to call the result significant.

```{r}
#| label: rev-her2st-benchmark
#| eval: true
# Random-pair benchmark for (c), 1,000 expression-matched gene pairs per axis, pooled over the 8 primary patients
her2_shared <- Reduce(intersect, lapply(her2_secs[her2_primary], function(s) rownames(s$expr)))
her2_mean <- Reduce(`+`, lapply(her2_secs[her2_primary], function(s) Matrix::rowSums(s$expr[her2_shared, ]))) /
  sum(sapply(her2_secs[her2_primary], function(s) ncol(s$expr)))
her2_universe <- her2_shared[Reduce(`&`, lapply(her2_secs[her2_primary], function(s) Matrix::rowMeans(s$expr[her2_shared, ] > 0) >= 0.01))]
her2_ecdf <- ecdf(her2_mean[her2_universe])
her2_pct <- her2_ecdf(her2_mean[her2_universe])
her2_pools <- lapply(setNames(spatial_axis_genes, spatial_axis_genes), function(g) {
  setdiff(her2_universe[abs(her2_pct - her2_ecdf(her2_mean[g])) <= 0.025], spatial_axis_genes)
})

her2_niches <- lapply(her2_secs[her2_primary], function(s) {
  A <- ring_adjacency(s, 0:1)
  lapply(setNames(seq_len(nrow(her2_axes)), her2_axes$axis_id), function(k) axis_niche(s, her2_axes[k, ], A))
})
her2_nb <- lapply(her2_secs[her2_primary], function(s) {
  A <- ring_adjacency(s, 0:1)
  sweep(as.matrix(s$expr[intersect(c(spatial_axis_genes, unlist(her2_pools)), rownames(s$expr)), ] %*% t(A)), 2, rowSums(A), "/")
})

her2_pooled_g <- function(axis_id, lig, rec) {
  gs <- bind_rows(lapply(her2_primary, function(sid) {
    nc <- her2_niches[[sid]][[axis_id]]
    if (!nc$estimable) return(data.frame(est = NA_real_, var = NA_real_))
    m <- her2_nb[[sid]]
    score <- if (length(lig) == 0) colMeans(m[rec, , drop = FALSE]) else m[lig, ] * colMeans(m[rec, , drop = FALSE])
    hedges_g(score, nc$niche)
  }))
  pool_sections(gs$est, gs$var)$est
}

set.seed(42)
her2_bench <- bind_rows(lapply(c("fn1_itga5_itgb1", "ccl5_ackr1"), function(ax_id) {
  ax <- her2_axes[her2_axes$axis_id == ax_id, ]
  rec_genes <- strsplit(ax$receptor, "_")[[1]]
  g <- unlist(lapply(1:1000, function(j) {
    lig <- sample(her2_pools[[ax$ligand]], 1)
    rec <- vapply(rec_genes, function(r) sample(setdiff(her2_pools[[r]], lig), 1), character(1))
    her2_pooled_g(ax_id, lig, rec)
  }))
  obs <- her2_test_pool(her2_primary_res) %>% filter(axis_id == ax_id, test == "(c) L-R co-expression") %>% pull(est)
  data.frame(axis_id = ax_id, observed_g = obs, null_median = median(g, na.rm = TRUE),
             percentile = 100 * mean(g < obs, na.rm = TRUE), emp_p = (1 + sum(g >= obs, na.rm = TRUE)) / (sum(is.finite(g)) + 1))
}))
write_csv(her2_bench, file.path(her2_res_dir, "her2st_benchmark_random_pairs.csv"))
knitr::kable(her2_bench %>% transmute(Axis = axis_labels[axis_id], `Observed g` = round(observed_g, 3), `Null median` = round(null_median, 3),
                                     Percentile = round(percentile, 1), `Empirical p (one-sided)` = signif(emp_p, 3)),
             caption = "HER2ST (c) against 1,000 expression-matched random gene pairs per axis")
```

The per-patient estimates next to the Wu pooled estimates show how close the two datasets are (@fig-her2st-forest).

```{r}
#| label: fig-her2st-forest
#| eval: true
#| fig-cap: "HER2ST tests of the lead axes: per-patient estimates (one section per patient) with 95% CI, the pooled HER2ST estimate, and the pooled Wu Visium estimate for the same test."
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 8
her2_forest_df <- bind_rows(
  her2_primary_res %>% transmute(axis_id, test, source = section, est, lo = est - 1.96 * sqrt(var), hi = est + 1.96 * sqrt(var)),
  declared %>% transmute(axis_id, test, source = "HER2ST pooled", est, lo, hi),
  spatial_pooled %>% filter(axis_id %in% her2_axes$axis_id) %>% transmute(axis_id, test, source = "Wu pooled", est, lo, hi)
) %>%
  mutate(
    across(c(est, lo, hi), ~ ifelse(test == "(a) weight correlation", tanh(.x), .x)),
    Axis = factor(axis_labels[axis_id], levels = axis_labels),
    group = case_when(source == "HER2ST pooled" ~ "HER2ST pooled", source == "Wu pooled" ~ "Wu pooled", TRUE ~ "HER2ST patient"),
    source = factor(source, levels = rev(c(her2_primary, "HER2ST pooled", "Wu pooled"))),
    test = recode(test, "(a) weight correlation" = "(a) Spearman rho", "(b) neighborhood enrichment" = "(b) log2 O/E co-occurrence",
                  "(c) L-R co-expression" = "(c) L-R Hedges' g")
  )
ggplot(her2_forest_df %>% filter(is.finite(est)), aes(x = est, y = source, color = group)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), width = 0.25, orientation = "y") +
  geom_point(aes(size = group != "HER2ST patient", shape = group != "HER2ST patient")) +
  facet_grid(Axis ~ test, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("HER2ST patient" = "#0072B2", "HER2ST pooled" = "black", "Wu pooled" = "#D55E00"), name = NULL) +
  scale_size_manual(values = c("FALSE" = 1.8, "TRUE" = 3), guide = "none") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("FALSE" = 16, "TRUE" = 18), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "Effect (95% CI)", y = NULL) +
  theme_publication() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
ggsave(file.path(her2_res_dir, "fig_her2st_forest.png"), last_plot(), width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 300)
```

The HER2ST maps for one patient show the same four panels as for Visium. The representative patient is the one whose primary section has the CCL5-ACKR1 co-expression effect closest to the pooled HER2ST estimate (@fig-her2st-maps).

```{r}
#| label: her2st-maps-setup
#| eval: true
her2_rep <- her2_primary_res %>%
  filter(axis_id == "ccl5_ackr1", test == "(c) L-R co-expression", is.finite(est)) %>%
  left_join(declared %>% filter(axis_id == "ccl5_ackr1", test == "(c) L-R co-expression") %>% select(axis_id, pooled = est), by = "axis_id") %>%
  slice_min(abs(est - pooled), n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
her2_rep_section <- her2_rep$section

# H&E in full-resolution pixel coordinates, downsampled for plotting, so that it lines up with the spot maps
her2_he_panel <- function(sid, title) {
  img <- jpeg::readJPEG(file.path("data/spatial/her2st/images_he/images/HE", paste0(sid, ".jpg")))
  step <- 4
  img <- img[seq(1, dim(img)[1], by = step), seq(1, dim(img)[2], by = step), , drop = FALSE]
  sp <- her2_secs[[sid]]$spots
  pad <- 200
  ggplot() +
    annotation_raster(img, xmin = 0, xmax = dim(img)[2] * step, ymin = -dim(img)[1] * step, ymax = 0) +
    coord_fixed(xlim = range(sp$pixel_x) + c(-pad, pad), ylim = -rev(range(sp$pixel_y)) + c(-pad, pad), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme_void(base_size = 13) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))
}
her2_spot_map <- function(sec, values, title, palette = "magma") {
  ggplot(data.frame(x = sec$spots$pixel_x, y = -sec$spots$pixel_y, v = values), aes(x = x, y = y, color = v)) +
    geom_point(size = 1.4) +
    scale_color_viridis_c(option = palette, name = NULL) +
    coord_fixed(xlim = range(sec$spots$pixel_x) + c(-200, 200), ylim = -rev(range(sec$spots$pixel_y)) + c(-200, 200), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme_void(base_size = 13) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5), legend.key.height = unit(0.6, "cm"), legend.key.width = unit(0.35, "cm"))
}
her2_axis_row <- function(ax, sid) {
  sec <- her2_secs[[sid]]
  A <- ring_adjacency(sec, 0:1)
  lr <- nb_mean(A, gene_score(sec$expr, ax$ligand)) * nb_mean(A, gene_score(sec$expr, ax$receptor))
  her2_he_panel(sid, sprintf("H&E (%s)", sid)) +
    her2_spot_map(sec, sec$w[, ax$sender], paste("Sender:", ax$sender), "viridis") +
    her2_spot_map(sec, sec$w[, ax$receiver], paste("Receiver:", ax$receiver), "viridis") +
    her2_spot_map(sec, lr, sprintf("%s x %s (neighborhood)", ax$ligand, gsub("_", "/", ax$receptor)), "magma") +
    plot_layout(nrow = 1)
}
her2_maps <- wrap_plots(lapply(seq_len(nrow(her2_axes)), function(k) her2_axis_row(her2_axes[k, ], her2_rep_section)), ncol = 1)
ggsave(file.path(her2_res_dir, "fig_her2st_maps.png"), her2_maps, width = 14, height = 7.6, dpi = 300)
```

# Clinical associations

Does axis co-expression in bulk tumors relate to patient outcome? The outcome is overall survival in three bulk cohorts: TCGA-BRCA and METABRIC first, and SCAN-B as an independent validation. This section describes the bulk data, the primary analysis, the secondary and exploratory analyses, the control for tumor composition, the SCAN-B replication, and the link to the downstream programs.

## Bulk expression and clinical data

For TCGA-BRCA and METABRIC we extract the axis genes from the expression matrices, with the legacy symbols DARC and IL8 mapped to ACKR1 and CXCL8. TCGA RSEM values are scaled to counts per million and log2-transformed. METABRIC values are the log-intensity microarray values as released. The `ITGA5_ITGB1` receptor is the mean of the log2 ITGA5 and ITGB1 values, and the ligand-receptor co-expression score of an axis is the mean of the log2 ligand and receptor values.

```{r}
#| label: clinical-processing
#| eval: false
# Target genes list to extract
target_genes <- c("CXCL12", "CXCR4", "CCL5", "CXCL8", "ACKR1", "MDK", "LRP1", "FN1", "ITGA5", "ITGB1", "APP", "CD74")

extract_target_genes <- function(mat, target_genes) {
  df_list <- list()
  for (gene in target_genes) {
    if (gene %in% rownames(mat)) {
      df_list[[gene]] <- mat[gene, ]
    } else if (gene == "ACKR1" && "DARC" %in% rownames(mat)) {
      df_list[[gene]] <- mat["DARC", ]
    } else if (gene == "CXCL8" && "IL8" %in% rownames(mat)) {
      df_list[[gene]] <- mat["IL8", ]
    } else {
      df_list[[gene]] <- rep(NA, ncol(mat))
    }
  }
  df <- as.data.frame(df_list)
  rownames(df) <- colnames(mat)
  return(df)
}

dir.create("objects/phase2", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

expr_tcga_raw <- fread("data/ext/brca_tcga/data_mrna_seq_v2_rsem.txt")

# Clean genes
expr_tcga_raw <- expr_tcga_raw[Hugo_Symbol != "" & !is.na(Hugo_Symbol)]
expr_tcga_raw <- expr_tcga_raw[!duplicated(Hugo_Symbol)]
genes_tcga <- expr_tcga_raw$Hugo_Symbol
mat_tcga <- as.matrix(expr_tcga_raw[, -c("Hugo_Symbol", "Entrez_Gene_Id"), with=FALSE])
rownames(mat_tcga) <- genes_tcga
colnames(mat_tcga) <- gsub("\\.", "-", colnames(mat_tcga))

mat_tcga <- apply(mat_tcga, 2, function(x) {
  s <- sum(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (s > 0) (x / s) * 1e6 else x
})

qs_save(mat_tcga, "objects/phase2/mat_tcga.qs2")

expr_tcga_targets <- extract_target_genes(mat_tcga, target_genes)
expr_tcga_targets$sampleId <- rownames(expr_tcga_targets)

# Log2 transformation
max_tcga_val <- max(expr_tcga_targets[, target_genes], na.rm = TRUE)
if (max_tcga_val > 100) {
  for (g in target_genes) {
    expr_tcga_targets[[g]] <- log2(expr_tcga_targets[[g]] + 1)
  }
}
if (all(c("ITGA5", "ITGB1") %in% colnames(expr_tcga_targets))) {
  expr_tcga_targets$ITGA5_ITGB1 <- rowMeans(expr_tcga_targets[, c("ITGA5", "ITGB1")], na.rm = TRUE)
}

cl_sample_tcga <- fread("data/ext/brca_tcga/data_clinical_sample.txt", header = TRUE, skip = "PATIENT_ID")
cl_patient_tcga <- fread("data/ext/brca_tcga/data_clinical_patient.txt", header = TRUE, skip = "PATIENT_ID")
cl_tcga <- merge(cl_sample_tcga, cl_patient_tcga, by = "PATIENT_ID")

tcga_base <- inner_join(cl_tcga, expr_tcga_targets, by = c("SAMPLE_ID" = "sampleId")) %>%
  rename(sampleId = SAMPLE_ID)

qs_save(tcga_base, "objects/phase2/clinical_tcga_base.qs2")

expr_meta_raw <- fread("data/ext/brca_metabric/data_mrna_illumina_microarray.txt")

# Clean genes
expr_meta_raw <- expr_meta_raw[Hugo_Symbol != "" & !is.na(Hugo_Symbol)]
expr_meta_raw <- expr_meta_raw[!duplicated(Hugo_Symbol)]
genes_meta <- expr_meta_raw$Hugo_Symbol
mat_meta <- as.matrix(expr_meta_raw[, -c("Hugo_Symbol", "Entrez_Gene_Id"), with=FALSE])
rownames(mat_meta) <- genes_meta

qs_save(mat_meta, "objects/phase2/mat_meta.qs2")

expr_meta_targets <- extract_target_genes(mat_meta, target_genes)
expr_meta_targets$sampleId <- rownames(expr_meta_targets)

# Log2 transformation
max_meta_val <- max(expr_meta_targets[, target_genes], na.rm = TRUE)
if (max_meta_val > 100) {
  for (g in target_genes) {
    expr_meta_targets[[g]] <- log2(expr_meta_targets[[g]] + 1)
  }
}
if (all(c("ITGA5", "ITGB1") %in% colnames(expr_meta_targets))) {
  expr_meta_targets$ITGA5_ITGB1 <- rowMeans(expr_meta_targets[, c("ITGA5", "ITGB1")], na.rm = TRUE)
}

cl_sample_meta <- fread("data/ext/brca_metabric/data_clinical_sample.txt", header = TRUE, skip = "PATIENT_ID")
cl_patient_meta <- fread("data/ext/brca_metabric/data_clinical_patient.txt", header = TRUE, skip = "PATIENT_ID")
cl_meta <- merge(cl_sample_meta, cl_patient_meta, by = "PATIENT_ID")

metabric_base <- inner_join(cl_meta, expr_meta_targets, by = c("SAMPLE_ID" = "sampleId")) %>%
  rename(sampleId = SAMPLE_ID)

qs_save(metabric_base, "objects/phase2/clinical_metabric_base.qs2")
```

Tumor composition is estimated from the same expression matrices with ESTIMATE (stromal, immune and ESTIMATE scores and tumor purity) and with CIBERSORT against the LM22 signature of 22 immune cell subsets, through `immunedeconv`. Missing values in the METABRIC matrix are replaced by the gene mean before CIBERSORT. The estimates are joined to the clinical tables.

```{r}
#| label: clinical-deconvolution
#| eval: false


# Register CIBERSORT binary and LM22 signature matrix
set_cibersort_binary("data/ext/CIBERSORT.R")
set_cibersort_mat("data/ext/LM22.txt")

mat_tcga <- qs_read("objects/phase2/mat_tcga.qs2")
mat_meta <- qs_read("objects/phase2/mat_meta.qs2")

tcga_base <- qs_read("objects/phase2/clinical_tcga_base.qs2")
metabric_base <- qs_read("objects/phase2/clinical_metabric_base.qs2")

# TCGA Deconvolution (ESTIMATE + CIBERSORT via immunedeconv)
est_tcga <- deconvolute_estimate(mat_tcga)
est_tcga_df <- as.data.frame(t(est_tcga))
est_tcga_df$sampleId <- rownames(est_tcga_df)
colnames(est_tcga_df) <- c("stromal_score", "immune_score", "ESTIMATEScore", "TumorPurity", "sampleId")

# CIBERSORT (LM22)
res_cib_tcga <- deconvolute(mat_tcga, method = "cibersort")
cib_tcga_df <- as.data.frame(t(res_cib_tcga[, -1]))
colnames(cib_tcga_df) <- res_cib_tcga$cell_type
cib_tcga_df$sampleId <- rownames(cib_tcga_df)

# Join TCGA base data with ESTIMATE & CIBERSORT
tcga_data <- tcga_base %>%
  left_join(est_tcga_df, by = "sampleId") %>%
  left_join(cib_tcga_df, by = "sampleId")

qs_save(tcga_data, "objects/phase2/clinical_tcga_processed.qs2")

# METABRIC Deconvolution (ESTIMATE + CIBERSORT via immunedeconv)
est_meta <- deconvolute_estimate(mat_meta)
est_meta_df <- as.data.frame(t(est_meta))
est_meta_df$sampleId <- rownames(est_meta_df)
colnames(est_meta_df) <- c("stromal_score", "immune_score", "ESTIMATEScore", "TumorPurity", "sampleId")

# CIBERSORT (LM22) - Clean NAs in mat_meta for CIBERSORT
mat_meta_clean <- mat_meta
for (i in which(rowSums(is.na(mat_meta_clean)) > 0)) {
  m <- mean(mat_meta_clean[i, ], na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.na(m)) m <- 0
  mat_meta_clean[i, is.na(mat_meta_clean[i, ])] <- m
}
res_cib_meta <- deconvolute(mat_meta_clean, method = "cibersort")
cib_meta_df <- as.data.frame(t(res_cib_meta[, -1]))
colnames(cib_meta_df) <- res_cib_meta$cell_type
cib_meta_df$sampleId <- rownames(cib_meta_df)

# Join METABRIC base data with ESTIMATE & CIBERSORT
metabric_data <- metabric_base %>%
  left_join(est_meta_df, by = "sampleId") %>%
  left_join(cib_meta_df, by = "sampleId")

qs_save(metabric_data, "objects/phase2/clinical_metabric_processed.qs2")
```
