
The immune-score correlations are shared across axes and most are large: for CCL5-ACKR1 they are `r sprintf("%.2f", pick(deconv, "r", axis_id = "ccl5_ackr1", feature = "immune_score", cohort = "TCGA"))` in TCGA and `r sprintf("%.2f", pick(deconv, "r", axis_id = "ccl5_ackr1", feature = "immune_score", cohort = "METABRIC"))` in METABRIC, for APP-CD74 `r sprintf("%.2f", pick(deconv, "r", axis_id = "app_cd74", feature = "immune_score", cohort = "TCGA"))` and `r sprintf("%.2f", pick(deconv, "r", axis_id = "app_cd74", feature = "immune_score", cohort = "METABRIC"))`, and for CXCL12-CXCR4 `r sprintf("%.2f", pick(deconv, "r", axis_id = "cxcl12_cxcr4", feature = "immune_score", cohort = "TCGA"))` and `r sprintf("%.2f", pick(deconv, "r", axis_id = "cxcl12_cxcr4", feature = "immune_score", cohort = "METABRIC"))`. A general "immune-rich" pattern is therefore not specific to CCL5-ACKR1. The CD8+ T-cell contrast is. Only CCL5-ACKR1 keeps a moderate to large positive CD8+ correlation (`r sprintf("%.2f", pick(deconv, "r", axis_id = "ccl5_ackr1", feature = "T cell CD8+", cohort = "TCGA"))` in TCGA and `r sprintf("%.2f", pick(deconv, "r", axis_id = "ccl5_ackr1", feature = "T cell CD8+", cohort = "METABRIC"))` in METABRIC), and it remains after the adjustment for purity (partial r `r sprintf("%.2f", pick(deconv, "partial_r_purity", axis_id = "ccl5_ackr1", feature = "T cell CD8+", cohort = "TCGA"))` and `r sprintf("%.2f", pick(deconv, "partial_r_purity", axis_id = "ccl5_ackr1", feature = "T cell CD8+", cohort = "METABRIC"))`). FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1 is the only axis that is negative in both cohorts (`r sprintf("%.2f", pick(deconv, "r", axis_id = "fn1_itga5_itgb1", feature = "T cell CD8+", cohort = "TCGA"))` and `r sprintf("%.2f", pick(deconv, "r", axis_id = "fn1_itga5_itgb1", feature = "T cell CD8+", cohort = "METABRIC"))`), and the correlation becomes clearly negative after adjustment for purity (partial r `r sprintf("%.2f", pick(deconv, "partial_r_purity", axis_id = "fn1_itga5_itgb1", feature = "T cell CD8+", cohort = "TCGA"))` and `r sprintf("%.2f", pick(deconv, "partial_r_purity", axis_id = "fn1_itga5_itgb1", feature = "T cell CD8+", cohort = "METABRIC"))`). It also has the largest purity-independent stromal correlation (partial r `r sprintf("%.2f", pick(deconv, "partial_r_purity", axis_id = "fn1_itga5_itgb1", feature = "stromal_score", cohort = "TCGA"))` and `r sprintf("%.2f", pick(deconv, "partial_r_purity", axis_id = "fn1_itga5_itgb1", feature = "stromal_score", cohort = "METABRIC"))`). The correlation with M2 macrophages is small and negative for CCL5-ACKR1 in TCGA and moderate in METABRIC, and negligible to small for FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1.

We read this as an opposing pattern in the CD8+ T-cell fraction and in stromal content: the CCL5-ACKR1 co-expression score marks T-cell-rich tumors and the FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1 score marks stroma-rich, CD8+-poor tumors. That is a bulk result. We do not see T-cell exclusion around FN1-high stroma in the spatial data, so any statement about immune exclusion rests on the bulk CD8+ association alone.

# Druggability

For the five axes we query the current release of DGIdb through its GraphQL API for the eleven axis genes: DGIdb v5.0.12, queried on 2026-10-01. The raw response is saved with the release number and the query date. The drug-gene table is rebuilt only from what DGIdb returns.

```{r}
#| label: rev-dgidb-query
#| eval: true
dgidb_raw_path <- "results/revision/dgidb_raw_response.json"
dgidb_genes <- c("CCL5", "ACKR1", "FN1", "ITGA5", "ITGB1", "CXCL12", "CXCR4", "MDK", "LRP1", "APP", "CD74")

if (!file.exists(dgidb_raw_path)) {
  gql <- sprintf(
    '{ serviceInfo { name version } genes(names: [%s]) { nodes { name conceptId interactions { drug { name conceptId approved antiNeoplastic } interactionScore interactionTypes { type directionality } sources { sourceDbName sourceDbVersion } publications { pmid } } } } }',
    paste0('"', dgidb_genes, '"', collapse = ", ")
  )
  resp <- httr::POST("https://dgidb.org/api/graphql", body = list(query = gql), encode = "json")
  dgidb_json <- jsonlite::fromJSON(httr::content(resp, as = "text", encoding = "UTF-8"), simplifyVector = FALSE)
  dgidb_json$query_date <- as.character(Sys.Date())
  writeLines(jsonlite::toJSON(dgidb_json, auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE), dgidb_raw_path)
}
dgidb_json <- jsonlite::fromJSON(dgidb_raw_path, simplifyVector = FALSE)

dgidb_df <- bind_rows(lapply(dgidb_json$data$genes$nodes, function(g) {
  bind_rows(lapply(g$interactions, function(x) {
    data.frame(
      gene = g$name,
      drug = x$drug$name,
      drug_concept = x$drug$conceptId,
      approved = isTRUE(x$drug$approved),
      antineoplastic = isTRUE(x$drug$antiNeoplastic),
      interaction_type = paste(unique(vapply(x$interactionTypes, function(t) t$type, character(1))), collapse = "; "),
      sources = paste(unique(vapply(x$sources, function(s) paste0(s$sourceDbName, " (", s$sourceDbVersion, ")"), character(1))), collapse = "; "),
      n_sources = length(x$sources),
      pmids = paste(unique(vapply(x$publications, function(p) as.character(p$pmid), character(1))), collapse = "; "),
      interaction_score = x$interactionScore
    )
  }))
})) %>%
  mutate(interaction_type = na_if(interaction_type, "")) %>%
  arrange(gene, desc(interaction_score))
write_csv(dgidb_df, "results/revision/dgidb_interactions_all.csv")

dgidb_release <- tibble::tibble(
  Service = dgidb_json$data$serviceInfo$name,
  Version = dgidb_json$data$serviceInfo$version,
  `Query date` = dgidb_json$query_date,
  `Genes queried` = paste(dgidb_genes, collapse = ", "),
  `Interactions returned` = nrow(dgidb_df)
)
write_csv(dgidb_release, "results/revision/dgidb_release.csv")
knitr::kable(dgidb_release, caption = "DGIdb release used for the drug-gene table")
knitr::kable(dgidb_df %>% count(gene, name = "interactions") %>% left_join(dgidb_df %>% group_by(gene) %>% summarise(approved = sum(approved), antineoplastic = sum(antineoplastic)), by = "gene"),
             caption = "DGIdb interactions per axis gene")

published_s5 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~gene, ~drug_published,
  "APP", "MEMANTINE",
  "APP", "DONEPEZIL",
  "CD74", "MILATUZUMAB",
  "CD74", "ST-1839",
  "FN1", "VATALANIB",
  "FN1", "VOLOCIXIMAB",
  "ITGA5", "VOLOCIXIMAB",
  "ITGA5", "ATN-161",
  "ITGB1", "OS225",
  "ACKR1", "CHLOROQUINE"
)
s5_check <- published_s5 %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    returned_by_dgidb = any(dgidb_df$gene == gene & grepl(drug_published, dgidb_df$drug, fixed = TRUE)),
    dgidb_sources = paste(dgidb_df$sources[dgidb_df$gene == gene & grepl(drug_published, dgidb_df$drug, fixed = TRUE)], collapse = " | "),
    same_drug_other_axis_genes = paste(setdiff(dgidb_df$gene[grepl(drug_published, dgidb_df$drug, fixed = TRUE)], gene), collapse = ", ")
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
write_csv(s5_check, "results/revision/dgidb_published_s5_check.csv")
knitr::kable(s5_check, caption = "Drug-gene pairs often cited for the axis genes, checked against the current DGIdb release")

# One row per gene-drug name; DGIdb returns separate records for some drug concepts
s5_rebuilt <- dgidb_df %>%
  group_by(gene, drug) %>%
  summarise(
    approved = any(approved),
    antineoplastic = any(antineoplastic),
    interaction_type = paste(sort(unique(na.omit(unlist(strsplit(interaction_type, "; "))))), collapse = "; "),
    sources = paste(sort(unique(unlist(strsplit(sources, "; ")))), collapse = "; "),
    pmids = paste(sort(unique(na_if(unlist(strsplit(pmids, "; ")), ""))), collapse = "; "),
    max_interaction_score = max(interaction_score),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(interaction_type = na_if(interaction_type, ""), pmids = na_if(pmids, "")) %>%
  arrange(gene, desc(max_interaction_score))
write_csv(s5_rebuilt, "results/revision/table_S5_rebuilt.csv")
knitr::kable(s5_rebuilt %>% filter(gene %in% c("CCL5", "ACKR1", "FN1", "ITGA5", "ITGB1")), digits = 2,
             caption = "Drug-gene table, lead-axis genes (all genes in table_S5_rebuilt.csv)")
DT::datatable(dgidb_df, filter = "top", rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 15, scrollX = TRUE),
              caption = "All DGIdb interactions for the axis genes (current release)")
```

DGIdb returned `r nrow(dgidb_df)` interaction records for the eleven genes. Five drug-gene pairs that are often cited for these genes (vatalanib, OS225, ST-1839, memantine and donepezil) are not returned by DGIdb, so they are not listed. DGIdb returns volociximab, an antibody against α5β1, under ITGA5 and ITGB1 (from GuideToPharmacology, ChEMBL and TALC) and not under FN1, and ATN-161, a peptide antagonist, under ITGA5 and ITGB1 from ChEMBL. Milatuzumab is returned for CD74. Chloroquine is listed for ACKR1 only through TTD 2020, without an interaction type or a publication, and it reflects the role of the Duffy antigen in *Plasmodium vivax* invasion and not a modulation of ACKR1's chemokine function. The other ACKR1 entries are the antimalarial AQ-13 and clozapine, which is a pharmacogenomic association with Duffy-null neutropenia. DGIdb therefore lists no compound that modulates the chemokine function of ACKR1. The entries that DGIdb returns for FN1 itself are the fibronectin extra-domain-B-targeting L19 immunoconjugates: L19-IL2 (darleukin), L19-TNFα, radretumab (L19-¹³¹I), onfekafusp alfa and AS1409. Volociximab and ATN-161 stopped at early-phase trials, so we do not treat them as candidates for repurposing.

# Summary

We integrated three single-cell cohorts of primary breast cancer (74 tumors) with two ligand-receptor frameworks and obtained a consensus of `r nrow(merged_df)` interactions that are conserved across cohorts and methods. After a general rule that removes promiscuous single-chain matrix receptors, five receptor-specific axes rank first to fifth, and they stay there across 12 alternative sketches of the data. We then asked what each axis is associated with.

```{r}
#| label: summary-table
#| eval: true
summary_table <- tibble::tibble(axis_id = candidate_registry$axis_id) %>%
  mutate(
    Axis = axis_labels[axis_id],
    `Pooled OS, double-high (TCGA + METABRIC)` = vapply(axis_id, function(a) paste0(hr_text(primary_pooled, axis_id = a), ", q = ", signif(pick(primary_pooled, "q_bh", axis_id = a), 2)), character(1)),
    `Pooled OS per SD, continuous score` = vapply(axis_id, function(a) paste0(hr_text(s4, axis_id = a), ", q = ", signif(pick(s4, "q_bh", axis_id = a), 2)), character(1)),
    `Three cohorts, continuous score` = vapply(axis_id, function(a) hr_text(pooled_3, axis_id = a, family = "C2 continuous"), character(1)),
    `FDR genes in pooled pseudobulk` = vapply(axis_id, function(a) as.character(pick(pooled_summary, "degs_fdr05", axis_id = a)), character(1))
  ) %>%
  select(-axis_id)
knitr::kable(summary_table, caption = "Evidence for the five axes in the bulk cohorts and in the pooled pseudobulk analysis.")
```

**FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1** has the clearest adverse association with overall survival. In the primary analysis of TCGA-BRCA and METABRIC, double-high tumors have a hazard ratio of `r hr_text(primary_pooled, axis_id = "fn1_itga5_itgb1")` (BH q = `r sg(pick(primary_pooled, "q_bh", axis_id = "fn1_itga5_itgb1"), 2)`), with the same direction in both cohorts and no heterogeneity. SCAN-B gives a similar estimate (`r hr_text(three_cohort %>% rename(hr_fe = hr, lo_fe = lo, hi_fe = hi), axis_id = "fn1_itga5_itgb1", family = "C1 double-high", cohort = "SCAN-B")`, BH q = `r sg(pick(scanb_res, "q_bh", axis_id = "fn1_itga5_itgb1", family = "C1 double-high", analysis = "All records"), 2)`), the three cohorts together give `r hr_text(pooled_3, axis_id = "fn1_itga5_itgb1", family = "C1 double-high")`, and the association holds after multiple imputation, PAM50 stratification, as a continuous score and, for the continuous score, after adjustment for tumor composition; it points the same way for disease-specific survival in METABRIC (q = 0.054). In a model with both genes, FN1 carries most of the bulk signal, so the result marks a fibronectin-rich stromal and vascular state and does not show that the pairing of FN1 with α5β1 is prognostic. In single cells, FN1-high endothelium shows a basement-membrane and angiogenic remodeling program together with a reduced MHC-II program, FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1 communication is much stronger in tumors than in normal breast and is driven by fibroblast FN1, and fibroblasts and endothelial cells sit side by side in tissue, as expected for stroma. The FN1-ITGA5/ITGB1 score is the only one negatively correlated with CD8+ T-cell content in bulk tumors, but we did not see T-cell exclusion around FN1-high stroma in tissue, so immune exclusion remains a bulk observation.

**CCL5-ACKR1** is associated with better survival when scored as a continuous co-expression variable (`r hr_text(pooled_3, axis_id = "ccl5_ackr1", family = "C2 continuous")` per SD in the three cohorts, with no heterogeneity), and the association remains after adjustment for tumor composition. The dichotomized all-patient association is null in all three cohorts and is absorbed by immune and stromal content. Its luminal subgroup does not survive correction. In tissue, T cells co-localize with ACKR1-positive venular endothelium in all six Visium sections, with co-expression in those niches, which is the strongest spatial result. In the independent HER2ST cohort the same pattern is directionally consistent and nominally significant for co-expression, and it does not meet the significance criterion, so we describe it as supportive and not as a replication. ACKR1 does not signal, so we treat the axis as a reference for T-cell entry through venules, and no gene passes FDR below 0.05 in the pooled pseudobulk contrast.

**CXCL12-CXCR4, MDK-LRP1 and APP-CD74** are null in the primary survival analysis. APP-CD74 has a continuous-score association that differs in direction between cohorts and cannot be interpreted. The spatial and pseudobulk results for these axes are exploratory.

These results are observational. Single-cell inference gives candidate interactions and not demonstrated signaling. Bulk expression cannot separate a ligand from its receptor or one cell type from another, Visium spots hold several cells, the spatial analysis rests on six sections of which four overlap with the discovery cohort, and the per-cohort pseudobulk comparisons have little power. We therefore regard the two lead axes as prioritized candidates for experimental follow-up, and not as established mechanisms or treatment targets.

```{r}
#| label: composite-setup
#| eval: true
#| include: false
dir.create("figures/composite", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# A saved PNG with its print size in inches. `rows` keeps a horizontal band (fractions of the height), `trim`
# removes white margins down to `margin` pixels, `size` shrinks the panel inside its cell and `title` adds a title
read_panel <- function(path, rows = c(0, 1), dpi = 300, trim = FALSE, margin = 30, size = 1, title = NULL) {
  img <- png::readPNG(path)
  if (dim(img)[3] == 4) img <- img[, , 1:3]
  keep <- seq(floor(rows[1] * dim(img)[1]) + 1, floor(rows[2] * dim(img)[1]))
  img <- img[keep, , , drop = FALSE]
  if (trim) {
    ink <- apply(img, c(1, 2), min) < 0.97
    rr <- range(which(rowSums(ink) > 0)) + c(-margin, margin)
    cc <- range(which(colSums(ink) > 0)) + c(-margin, margin)
    img <- img[max(1, rr[1]):min(dim(img)[1], rr[2]), max(1, cc[1]):min(dim(img)[2], cc[2]), , drop = FALSE]
  }
  list(img = img, w = dim(img)[2] / dpi, h = dim(img)[1] / dpi, size = size, title = title)
}

# One panel as a patchwork element, drawn at a fraction of the cell width so that it keeps its print scale
panel_grob <- function(p, frac = p$size) {
  el <- wrap_elements(full = grid::rasterGrob(p$img, width = unit(frac, "npc"), interpolate = TRUE))
  if (!is.null(p$title)) el <- el + ggtitle(p$title) + theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))
  el
}

# Panels stacked, side by side or in a grid, with letters A, B, C, saved at 300 dpi. Stacked panels keep their print
# width against the widest one; side-by-side panels are scaled to a common height
save_composite <- function(panels, path, stack = TRUE, ncol = NULL) {
  ws <- vapply(panels, function(p) p$w, numeric(1))
  hs <- vapply(panels, function(p) p$h, numeric(1))
  if (!stack) {
    height <- max(hs)
    widths <- ws * height / hs
    grobs <- lapply(panels, panel_grob)
    layout <- plot_layout(nrow = 1, widths = widths)
    width <- sum(widths)
    n_rows <- 1
  } else if (is.null(ncol)) {
    width <- max(ws)
    grobs <- lapply(panels, function(p) panel_grob(p, p$w / width))
    layout <- plot_layout(ncol = 1, heights = hs)
    height <- sum(hs)
    n_rows <- length(panels)
  } else {
    width <- ncol * max(ws)
    grobs <- lapply(panels, panel_grob)
    n_rows <- ceiling(length(panels) / ncol)
    layout <- plot_layout(ncol = ncol)
    height <- max(hs) * n_rows
  }
  # Room for the panel letters, and for the panel titles when there are any
  pad <- 0.3 + if (any(vapply(panels, function(p) !is.null(p$title), logical(1)))) 0.35 else 0
  p <- wrap_plots(grobs) + layout +
    plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") & theme(plot.tag = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"))
  ggsave(path, p, width = width, height = height + pad * n_rows, dpi = 300, bg = "white", limitsize = FALSE)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: composite-spatial
#| eval: true
#| include: false
print_spot_map <- function(sec, values, title, legend, palette) {
  ggplot(data.frame(x = sec$spots$pxl_col, y = -sec$spots$pxl_row, v = values), aes(x = x, y = y, color = v)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.45) +
    scale_color_viridis_c(option = palette, name = legend) +
    coord_fixed(xlim = range(sec$spots$pxl_col) + c(-150, 150), ylim = -rev(range(sec$spots$pxl_row)) + c(-150, 150), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme_void(base_size = 13) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5), legend.title = element_text(size = 11),
          legend.text = element_text(size = 10), legend.key.height = unit(0.55, "cm"), legend.key.width = unit(0.3, "cm"))
}
print_he_panel <- function(sid) {
  img <- png::readPNG(file.path(spatial_dir, "spatial", paste0(sid, "_spatial"), "tissue_lowres_image.png"))
  sc <- visium[[sid]]$scalef$tissue_lowres_scalef
  sp <- visium[[sid]]$spots
  ggplot() +
    annotation_raster(img, xmin = 0, xmax = dim(img)[2] / sc, ymin = -dim(img)[1] / sc, ymax = 0) +
    coord_fixed(xlim = range(sp$pxl_col) + c(-150, 150), ylim = -rev(range(sp$pxl_row)) + c(-150, 150), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = paste0("H&E\n", sid)) +
    theme_void(base_size = 13) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))
}
print_axis_row <- function(axis, sid) {
  ax <- spatial_axes[spatial_axes$axis_id == axis, ]
  sec <- secs_primary[[sid]]
  A <- ring_adjacency(sec, 0:1)
  lr <- nb_mean(A, gene_score(sec$expr, ax$ligand)) * nb_mean(A, gene_score(sec$expr, ax$receptor))
  print_he_panel(sid) +
    print_spot_map(sec, sec$w[, ax$sender], paste0("Sender weight\n", print_cell_labels[ax$sender]), "Weight", "viridis") +
    print_spot_map(sec, sec$w[, ax$receiver], paste0("Receiver weight\n", print_cell_labels[ax$receiver]), "Weight", "viridis") +
    print_spot_map(sec, lr, sprintf("Co-expression\n%s × %s", ax$ligand, gsub("_", "/", ax$receptor)), "Score", "magma") +
    plot_layout(nrow = 1)
}
```
